zones.unescoReference: UNESCO WHC 121 - Bhaktapur Durbar Square Monument Zone
zones.description: Bhaktapur, Khwopa in Newar, is the best-preserved of the valley's three royal cities. Its Durbar Square, Taumadhi Square and Tachupal Square hold the five-roofed Nyatapola, the Palace of Fifty-Five Windows and the Golden Gate, and the municipality reinvests visitor fees in conservation and in living festivals such as Bisket Jatra.

walkingTour.title: Khwopa: Bhaktapur's Living Medieval City
walkingTour.startPoint: Siddha Pokhari, near the western city gate

zones.description: Boudhanath, Khasti in Newar, holds one of the largest stupas in the world on flat ground north-east of Kathmandu. Since 1959 Tibetan refugees, alongside Sherpa, Tamang and Newar communities, have built dozens of monasteries around its circular kora, making Boudha a global centre of Tibetan Buddhism. The stupa's spire, cracked in 2015, was rebuilt by the community and reconsecrated in 2016.

walkingTour.title: Boudha Kora: Stupa, Monasteries and Himalayan Life
walkingTour.titleNe: बौद्ध कोरा: स्तूप, गुम्बा र हिमाली जीवन
walkingTour.startPoint: Main southern gateway of Boudhanath Stupa

zones.unescoReference: UNESCO WHC 121 - Changu Narayan Monument Zone
zones.description: Changu Narayan crowns a ridge at the eastern edge of the Kathmandu Valley. Its two-tiered Vishnu temple, rebuilt in 1702, stands in a courtyard holding the valley's finest collection of Licchavi sculpture and Nepal's oldest dated inscription, carved for King Manadeva in 464 CE.

walkingTour.title: Changu Narayan: Fifteen Centuries of Vishnu
walkingTour.startPoint: Main gate of the Changu Narayan courtyard, top of Changu village

zones.nameEn: Hidden Gems: Kirtipur, Panauti, Bungamati and Satellite Towns
zones.nameNe: लुकेका सम्पदा: कीर्तिपुर, पनौती, बुंगमती र आसपासका सहर
zones.description: Beyond the famous squares, smaller Newar towns around the valley preserve heritage that receives a fraction of the visitors. Kirtipur's hilltop temples, the rain god's village of Bungamati and the oil-pressing village of Khokana, the riverside temples of Panauti, and the hill shrines of Sankhu and Pharping are the focus of efforts to spread visitors toward lesser-known sites.

walkingTour.title: Unseen Valley: Satellite Heritage Towns Circuit

zones.unescoReference: UNESCO WHC 121 - Hanuman Dhoka Durbar Square Monument Zone
zones.description: The former royal palace square of Kathmandu, where Malla kings and later the Shah dynasty ruled. It combines the Hanuman Dhoka palace, the city's namesake Kasthamandap pavilion, the residence of the living goddess Kumari and dozens of temples rebuilt or repaired after the 2015 Gorkha earthquake.

walkingTour.title: Royal Kathmandu: From Kasthamandap to Taleju

zones.description: Pashupatinath, on the banks of the sacred Bagmati river east of Kathmandu, is the holiest Hindu shrine in Nepal. Around the gilded temple of Shiva as lord of all creatures lie cremation ghats, forested slopes, Shiva shrines, ashrams and the Shakti Peeth of Guhyeshwari, managed by the Pashupati Area Development Trust. The main courtyard is open only to Hindus.

walkingTour.title: Pashupati: Temples, Ghats and the Circle of Life
walkingTour.startPoint: Western main gate of Pashupatinath Temple, Gaushala side

zones.unescoReference: UNESCO WHC 121 - Patan Durbar Square Monument Zone
zones.description: The palace square of the former Malla kingdom of Lalitpur, the city of beauty, renowned for its metalworkers and stone carvers. Its palace courtyards, the stone Krishna Mandir and the nearby Buddhist monasteries of Kwa Bahal and Mahabouddha show the intertwined Hindu and Buddhist heritage of Patan, much of it restored with the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust after 2015.

walkingTour.title: Patan: City of Artisans and Monasteries

zones.description: Swayambhu, Singu in Newar, crowns a hill west of Kathmandu and is one of the valley's oldest Buddhist sites, revered by Newar and Tibetan Buddhists and by Hindus. Its hilltop gathers the great stupa with its painted eyes, the vajra and twin shikharas of Pratap Malla, the Harati shrine and a crowd of votive chaityas, with monasteries on its slopes.

walkingTour.title: Swayambhu: The Hill of Self-Arisen Light

monuments.disambiguationTip: Nyatapola is the five-roofed temple on a towering plinth with stone guardians flanking its stairway; Bhairavnath next door is rectangular with three roofs.

lore.title: Bhupatindra's Masterpiece
lore.excerpt: Nyatapola, whose name means 'five-storeyed' in Newar, was built in 1702 by King Bhupatindra Malla of Bhaktapur, the most ambitious builder among the city's rulers. Rising about thirty metres, it is the tallest pagoda in Nepal and dominates Taumadhi Square. Bhu…

lore.excerpt: Nyatapola achieves its soaring height through a combination of a tall five-stage plinth and five diminishing roofs. A steep stone stairway climbs the plinth's central axis on the main side, flanked on each stage by pairs of stone guardians. The temple's brick …

lore.excerpt: The stone guardians lining Nyatapola's stairway are among the most famous sculptures in Nepal. At the bottom stand the legendary wrestlers Jayamal and Phattu, said to have possessed the strength of ten ordinary men. Above them stand elephants, each said to be …

lore.title: A Palace Rebuilt by a Builder King
lore.excerpt: The Palace of Fifty-Five Windows was the residence of the Malla kings of Bhaktapur. Its origins go back to the fifteenth century, when King Yaksha Malla ruled a unified valley from Bhaktapur, but its present form owes most to King Bhupatindra Malla, who remode…

lore.title: Fifty-Five Windows in a Row
lore.excerpt: The palace's name comes from the long row of carved wooden windows that runs along its upper floor, a single continuous band of lattice and frames that gives the facade its distinctive rhythm. Each window is a masterpiece of Newar joinery, with interlocking la…

lore.title: Windows as Sacred Frames

lore.title: Festivals Before the Palace
lore.excerpt: The palace faced the square where Bhaktapur's great festivals unfolded, and the king watched from its windows as masked dances, processions and chariots passed below. During Dashain, the palace's Taleju shrine became the focus of royal ritual, and during other…

lore.title: A Stone Temple for the Mother Goddess
lore.excerpt: Vatsala Durga is a stone shikhara temple in Bhaktapur Durbar Square, built in 1672 by King Jagat Prakash Malla and dedicated to Vatsala, a form of the mother goddess Durga. Its style follows the north Indian shikhara tradition that had become fashionable in th…

lore.title: Shikhara and Pavilion
lore.excerpt: Vatsala Durga rises on a stepped plinth in the form of a stone shikhara, a tapering tower surrounded at its base by small pavilions and pinnacles. The design echoes the Krishna Mandir in Patan but on a smaller scale, and its carved stone details show the skill…

lore.title: The Bell of Barking Dogs
lore.excerpt: The bell beside Vatsala Durga is famous as the 'bell of barking dogs'. According to local tradition, whenever the bell is rung, dogs in the square begin to bark and whine, and residents often say the sound disturbs them. Some explain the phenomenon by the bell…

lore.title: Worship of the Mother Goddess
lore.excerpt: Vatsala Durga receives daily worship, and her shrine is particularly important during Dashain, the great festival of Durga, when the goddess's victory over the buffalo demon Mahishasura is celebrated. During this festival Bhaktapur's squares fill with worshipp…

lore.excerpt: Vatsala Durga collapsed in the 2015 earthquake, its stone tower falling into a heap of masonry, and its loss was one of the most visible signs of the earthquake's impact on Bhaktapur Durbar Square. The bell beside it survived. Reconstruction began after carefu…

lore.title: A Rectangular Pagoda
lore.excerpt: Bhairavnath is a rectangular pagoda with three tiers, a less common form than the square plan used for most Newar temples. Its broad facade faces Taumadhi Square, and a small niche on the front holds a gilded image of Bhairav's head, through which offerings ar…

lore.title: The Head of Bhairav

lore.excerpt: Tachupal Square, where the Dattatreya temple stands, is the oldest part of Bhaktapur, and the temple is traditionally dated to 1427, during the reign of King Yaksha Malla, who ruled a unified Kathmandu Valley from Bhaktapur. Like Kasthamandap in Kathmandu, it …

lore.excerpt: The Dattatreya temple is a three-tiered pagoda raised on a plinth, distinguished by a projecting front section that forms a kind of porch, an unusual feature among Newar temples. Its stairway is guarded by statues of the wrestlers Jayamal and Phattu, the same …

lore.excerpt: Dattatreya is a composite deity who combines aspects of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, the creator, preserver and destroyer of the Hindu trinity. He is often depicted with three heads and six arms, carrying the emblems of each god, and accompanied by a cow and four…

monuments.disambiguationTip: Siddha Pokhari is the large open rectangular pond at the city's western edge; Naga Pokhari is a small stone tank inside the palace.

lore.title: The Great Pond at the City Gate
lore.excerpt: Siddha Pokhari is a large rectangular pond near the western entrance to Bhaktapur's old city, traditionally attributed to the fifteenth century and the reign of King Yaksha Malla. Ponds like this were essential to Newar towns: they stored rainwater, recharged …

lore.excerpt: Siddha Pokhari is a carefully engineered reservoir with stone and brick embankments, walkways and steps leading down to the water. Ponds in the Kathmandu Valley were connected to networks of canals and underground channels that distributed water to spouts and …

lore.excerpt: For centuries, pilgrims have walked from Bhaktapur to the hilltop temple of Changu Narayan, the oldest Vishnu temple in the valley, about six kilometres to the north. The route crosses farmland north of the city and climbs a forested ridge to the temple, which…

lore.title: Villages, Terraces and Wayside Shrines
lore.excerpt: The trail's architecture is that of the rural valley: terraced rice and vegetable fields, brick farmhouses, small Newar villages and wayside shrines. Along the way, walkers pass shrines to Ganesh, small chaityas and resting platforms called patis, where pilgri…

lore.title: Ganesh at the Start, Vishnu at the End
lore.excerpt: Pilgrimage routes in the Kathmandu Valley are marked by shrines that structure the journey. Ganesh, the remover of obstacles, is often worshipped at the start of a journey, and shrines to him appear at trailheads and crossroads. Along the route, small chaityas…

lore.title: Walking for Festivals and Vows
lore.excerpt: Pilgrims walk to Changu Narayan for festivals, especially on Ekadashi days sacred to Vishnu and during the month of Kartik, when Vishnu worship is particularly important. Some devotees make the journey to fulfil vows, walking barefoot or carrying offerings. In…

lore.title: Rural Heritage After 2015
lore.excerpt: The 2015 earthquake caused severe damage in the villages between Bhaktapur and Changu Narayan, destroying many traditional houses and damaging shrines and resting places. Reconstruction has been uneven: some households rebuilt in traditional styles with suppor…

monuments.audioHook: From here, an old pilgrim road leaves Bhaktapur and climbs north through rice terraces and brick villages to a hilltop temple about six kilometres away. That temple, Changu Narayan, is the oldest Vishnu temple in the valley, with sculptures carved some fifteen hundred years ago. Before buses, this was how Bhaktapur's f…
monuments.nepaliSummary: भक्तपुरदेखि चाँगुनारायणसम्मको पुरानो तीर्थ पदमार्ग खेत, नेवार गाउँ र वनबीच हुँदै करिब छ किलोमिटर उकालो लाग्छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: End the city walk by pointing pilgrims north toward Changu Narayan.

features: two-tiered temple with gilded roof elements in a residential square
Garuda pillars standing in front of the temple
monuments.disambiguationTip: Wakupati Narayan is a smaller two-roofed Vishnu temple with gilded roof elements and Garuda pillars; Dattatreya has three roofs and wrestler guardians.

lore.title: A Neighbourhood Temple of Vishnu
lore.excerpt: Wakupati Narayan is a temple of Vishnu in eastern Bhaktapur, near Tachupal Square, in one of the city's older residential neighbourhoods. Its precise founding date has not been firmly established in the published sources available to Saalik, and it is attribut…

lore.title: Gilded Roofs in a Quiet Square
lore.excerpt: Wakupati Narayan is a two-tiered pagoda with gilded metal elements on its roofs, which give it a bright appearance unusual for a neighbourhood temple. In front of the temple stand pillars topped by figures of Garuda, Vishnu's bird-mount, a common feature of Vi…

lore.title: Narayan and Garuda
lore.excerpt: Narayan, the form of Vishnu worshipped at this temple, is the preserver of the cosmic order, and his iconography includes the conch, discus, mace and lotus, which he holds in his four hands. Garuda, the eagle-like bird who carries Vishnu, appears on the pillar…

lore.title: Ekadashi and Neighbourhood Festivals
lore.excerpt: Wakupati Narayan receives daily worship from residents, and Ekadashi, the eleventh day of each lunar fortnight, brings additional devotees, since it is sacred to Vishnu. During the month of Kartik, Vishnu worship intensifies, with lamps lit and special rituals…

lore.title: Caring for Neighbourhood Heritage
lore.excerpt: Neighbourhood temples like Wakupati Narayan depend on local guthis and residents for their maintenance, often with support from Bhaktapur Municipality. The 2015 earthquake damaged many temples and houses in Bhaktapur's neighbourhoods, and restoration of smalle…

monuments.audioHook: Wander a few lanes away from the crowds, and you will find this two-roofed temple glinting with gold in a quiet square. Wakupati Narayan is a neighbourhood temple of Vishnu, and the stone birds kneeling on the pillars in front of it are Garudas, Vishnu's mounts. No royal founder is recorded in Saalik's sources, and the…
monuments.nepaliSummary: वाकुपति नारायण भक्तपुरको पूर्वी टोलमा रहेको सुनौला छाना र गरुड स्तम्भ भएको दुई तले विष्णु मन्दिर हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Show how neighbourhood guthis sustain temples beyond the main squares.

features: rectangular stone-lined bath tank inside the palace
upright stone naga column at the centre
monuments.disambiguationTip: Naga Pokhari is a small stone tank inside the Bhaktapur palace with a serpent rising from its centre; Tusha Hiti in Patan is a sunken stepped bath lined with deity niches.

lore.title: The Kings' Serpent Bath
lore.excerpt: Naga Pokhari is a royal bath tank within the Bhaktapur palace complex, reached through the Golden Gate. It is usually attributed to the seventeenth century, and some accounts associate it with King Jitamitra Malla, who reigned in the later part of that century…

lore.title: Stone, Water and Serpents
lore.excerpt: Naga Pokhari is a rectangular tank lined with stone, with steps leading down to the water and a gilded spout through which water enters. At the centre of the tank rises a stone column topped by a naga, a serpent spirit, its hood raised above the water. Smaller…

lore.title: Nagas, Guardians of Water
lore.excerpt: Nagas are serpent spirits who play a central role in the mythology of the Kathmandu Valley. Legend tells that the valley was once a lake inhabited by nagas, and that when the lake was drained, the nagas remained as guardians of water and rain. Their worship is…

lore.title: Purification Before Worship
lore.excerpt: Royal bathing at Naga Pokhari was a ritual act, part of the preparations for worshipping Taleju and for performing other ceremonies. Bathing in water protected by the nagas purified the body and mind, allowing the king or members of the royal family to approac…

lore.title: Keeping the Royal Bath Intact
lore.excerpt: Naga Pokhari's conservation requires attention to both its stonework and its water supply. Stone tanks can crack in earthquakes, and the 1934 and 2015 earthquakes both damaged the Bhaktapur palace complex. The bath's water supply depends on channels that may h…

monuments.audioHook: Pass through the Golden Gate into the palace and you will find a quiet stone tank with a serpent rising from the middle of the water. This is Naga Pokhari, the serpent pond, where Bhaktapur's royal family bathed before worshipping their goddess Taleju. Legend says the whole Kathmandu Valley was once a lake ruled by ser…
monuments.nepaliSummary: नाग पोखरी भक्तपुर दरबारभित्रको शाही स्नान कुण्ड हो, जसको बीचमा ढुङ्गाको नाग उठेको छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the valley-lake legend at the serpent bath.

features: inner palace courtyard reached through the Golden Gate
closed to non-Hindus and seen only from permitted exterior views
monuments.disambiguationTip: Taleju Chowk is Bhaktapur's restricted inner courtyard behind the Golden Gate; Patan's Mul Chowk is open to visitors and has gilded river goddesses at its golden door.

lore.title: The Goddess's Courtyard
lore.excerpt: Taleju Chowk is the courtyard of the royal goddess Taleju within the Bhaktapur palace, reached through the Golden Gate. It is the most sacred space in the palace complex and has been closed to non-Hindus for centuries. The cult of Taleju, the tutelary goddess …

lore.title: An Inner Sanctum of Carving
lore.excerpt: Because Taleju Chowk is closed to non-Hindus, most visitors know it only from descriptions and photographs. Published accounts describe a courtyard of exceptional richness, with carved and painted struts, doors and windows, gilded metalwork and shrines surroun…

lore.title: Taleju, Protector of Kings
lore.excerpt: Taleju is understood as a form of Durga, the warrior goddess, and she is closely associated with Tantric traditions. In Bhaktapur, as in the other Malla cities, her image is hidden from public view and served only by initiated priests. The courtyard's carvings…

lore.title: Dashain in Taleju Chowk
lore.excerpt: Taleju Chowk becomes the focus of Bhaktapur's most important royal rituals during Dashain, the autumn festival of the goddess Durga. Sacrifices are offered to Taleju by her priests, and the courtyard is the setting for ceremonies that once confirmed the king's…

lore.title: Conserving a Restricted Space
lore.excerpt: Conservation of Taleju Chowk presents special challenges because of its restricted access and active ritual use. Work must be coordinated with priests and carried out by craftsmen who are permitted to enter, and documentation is limited by rules about photogra…

monuments.audioHook: Stand at the Golden Gate and look through, as far as you are allowed. Beyond lies Taleju Chowk, the courtyard of the royal goddess of Bhaktapur, and for centuries no one but Hindu worshippers and her priests has stepped inside. Those who have describe carved and painted struts, gilded doors and shrines of extraordinary…
monuments.nepaliSummary: तलेजु चोक भक्तपुर दरबारभित्रको तलेजु देवीको पवित्र चोक हो, जहाँ गैरहिन्दूलाई प्रवेश निषेध छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Explain what lies behind the Golden Gate and why it stays closed.

monuments.century: pottery tradition of many centuries; square's buildings largely rebuilt after 1934 and 2015
features: open square filled with rows of clay pots drying in the sun
potters working wheels in the open air
monuments.disambiguationTip: Pottery Square is an open working square covered in drying pots south of Taumadhi; no temple dominates the frame.

lore.title: Centuries of Clay
lore.excerpt: Pottery Square, known in Newar as Talako, lies a short walk south of Taumadhi Square in Bhaktapur and is home to the city's community of potters, the Prajapati, who have worked clay here for many generations. Bhaktapur's pottery tradition is often described as…

lore.title: A Workshop Under the Sky
lore.excerpt: Pottery Square is less a monument than a working landscape. Its open paving is covered with rows of freshly shaped pots drying in the sun, while potters sit at wheels under awnings or in doorways, spinning clay into vessels with practised speed. Around the squ…

lore.title: Ganesh and the Potter's Wheel
lore.excerpt: For the potters of Bhaktapur, clay is not only a material but part of a sacred cycle. Ritual vessels made here are used in temples and homes for offerings of water, milk and grain, and oil lamps light shrines across the city during festivals such as Tihar. The…

lore.title: Lamps for Tihar, Jars for Weddings
lore.excerpt: Demand for pottery follows Bhaktapur's festival calendar. Before Tihar, the festival of lights in autumn, potters produce thousands of small oil lamps used to illuminate homes and temples. Weddings, funerals and other rites require specific vessels, some made …

lore.title: Sustaining a Living Craft
lore.excerpt: Conserving Pottery Square means sustaining both its buildings and its craft. The 2015 earthquake damaged houses and workshops around the square, and families rebuilt with varying support, sometimes in traditional styles and sometimes with concrete. The craft i…

monuments.audioHook: Follow the lanes south from Taumadhi Square until the ground in front of you is covered with rows of clay pots drying in the sun. Welcome to Pottery Square, where Bhaktapur's potters have shaped clay for generations. Watch a potter set the wheel spinning and pull a water jar out of a lump of earth in less than a minute…
monuments.nepaliSummary: भक्तपुरको कुमाले टोल (तलाको) मा पुस्तौंदेखि प्रजापति कुमालेहरूले माटाका भाँडा बनाउँदै आएका छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Watch the potters at work and connect craft with festival ritual.

monuments.century: Licchavi origins by chronicle tradition (5th-7th century CE); repeatedly enlarged
features: massive white dome on a three-tiered mandala platform
prayer flags radiating from the spire to the platform edge
circular kora street lined with monasteries and shops
monuments.disambiguationTip: Boudhanath's stupa is a vast dome on a stepped mandala platform at street level ringed by shops; Swayambhu's is smaller and sits on a crowded hilltop.

lore.title: Legends of Penance and Permission
lore.excerpt: Boudhanath, known to Newars as Khasti and to Tibetans as Jarung Khashor, is one of the largest stupas in the world and the heart of Tibetan Buddhist life in Nepal. Its origins are wrapped in legend. A Newar chronicle tradition tells that a Licchavi king, unkno…

lore.title: A Mandala in Brick and Whitewash
lore.excerpt: Boudhanath is built as a vast three-dimensional mandala. A three-tiered platform with projecting corners supports a massive hemispherical dome, crowned by a gilded square harmika painted with the eyes of the Buddha and a stepped spire. Seen from above, the pla…

lore.title: Eyes, Steps and Elements
lore.excerpt: Like Swayambhu, Boudhanath carries the painted eyes of the Buddha on each side of its harmika, symbolising all-seeing wisdom and compassion, with the numeral one in place of a nose. Its forms map the Buddhist path and the elements: the platform represents eart…

lore.title: The Evening Kora
lore.excerpt: Every day, but especially at dawn and dusk, thousands of people walk the kora, the clockwise circuit around the stupa. Tibetan grandmothers spinning hand-held prayer wheels, monks in maroon robes, Sherpa and Tamang families, Newar devotees and visitors from ar…

lore.title: Rebuilt in Eighteen Months
lore.excerpt: The 2015 earthquake cracked Boudhanath's harmika and spire, and the upper structure had to be dismantled for safety. What followed was one of the most remarkable reconstruction efforts in Nepal. The Boudhanath Area Development Committee, working with local Bud…

monuments.audioHook: Join the river of people walking clockwise around this enormous white dome. Tibetan grandmothers spin prayer wheels, monks chant under their breath, and above you the eyes of the Buddha gaze from the golden tower in all four directions. This is Boudhanath, one of the largest stupas on Earth. Tibetan legend says a humbl…
monuments.nepaliSummary: बौद्धनाथ स्तूप विश्वकै ठूला स्तूपमध्ये एक हो; २०१५ को भूकम्पपछि समुदायले यसको गजुर १८ महिनामै पुनर्निर्माण गरे।
monuments.talkingPoint: Explain both founding legends and the community rebuild of 2016.

monuments.century: date unconfirmed; Newar shrine tradition of the Malla centuries
features: small Newar-style shrine on the northern side of the stupa circuit
Newar pagoda form standing among Tibetan monastery facades
monuments.disambiguationTip: Boudha's Ajima shrine is a small Newar-style temple on the flat kora; Swayambhu's Harati is a gilded pagoda beside a hilltop stupa.

lore.title: A Newar Goddess on a Tibetan Circuit
lore.excerpt: On the northern side of the Boudhanath kora stands a small shrine to Ajima, the grandmother goddess identified with Hariti, protector of children. Its Newar architectural style contrasts with the Tibetan monasteries that surround it, a reminder that Boudha was…

lore.title: A Small Pagoda Among Gompas
lore.excerpt: The Ajima shrine is a compact Newar-style temple with brick walls, a carved doorway and a pagoda roof, set on the edge of the kora where it is easily missed among the shopfronts and monastery gates. Its scale is modest, but its form links it with the shrines o…

lore.title: The Grandmother Who Protects
lore.excerpt: Ajima, meaning 'grandmother' in Newar, is a name for a group of protective goddesses in the Kathmandu Valley, many of them identified with Hariti, the ogress converted by the Buddha into a protector of children. She is honoured especially by mothers and by fam…

lore.title: Pausing on the Kora
lore.excerpt: Many people walking the kora stop at the Ajima shrine to make offerings of flowers, rice, coins or red powder, ring the bell and touch the threshold before continuing their circuit. Newar families from the surrounding area bring children for blessings, and the…

lore.title: A Small Shrine in a Changing Neighbourhood
lore.excerpt: Boudha has changed dramatically since the 1960s, as Tibetan settlement, tourism and urban growth transformed a village around a stupa into a dense, busy neighbourhood. Small shrines like the Ajima temple are vulnerable in this setting, squeezed by new building…

monuments.audioHook: As you walk the kora, look for a small Newar-style temple tucked between the shops on the northern side. This is the shrine of Ajima, the grandmother goddess who protects children, and she was honoured here long before the Tibetan monasteries you see today were built. Many people say she is the protector of the great s…
monuments.nepaliSummary: बौद्ध कोराको उत्तरतिर रहेको अजिमा मन्दिर बालबालिकाकी रक्षक देवीको नेवारी शैलीको सानो मन्दिर हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Show Boudha's Newar layer before visiting the Tibetan monasteries.

features: shrine dedicated to Guru Rinpoche near the stupa circuit
large image of Padmasambhava visible through the doorway
monuments.disambiguationTip: Guru Lhakhang centres on a large Guru Rinpoche image; check the main image through the doorway to distinguish it from the neighbouring gompas.

lore.title: A Shrine to the Precious Guru
lore.excerpt: Guru Lhakhang, meaning 'temple of the Guru', is a shrine near the Boudhanath circuit dedicated to Guru Rinpoche, the eighth-century master Padmasambhava who is credited in Tibetan tradition with establishing Buddhism in Tibet. Padmasambhava is closely linked w…

lore.title: Tibetan Shrine Design
lore.excerpt: Guru Lhakhangs typically follow the design of a Tibetan temple hall, with a central image of Padmasambhava on an altar, flanked by his consorts or by other masters of the lineage. The walls are often painted with murals of deities and teachers, and the ceiling…

lore.title: The Lotus-Born Master
lore.excerpt: Padmasambhava, whose name means 'lotus-born', is depicted seated on a lotus, wearing a distinctive hat topped with a feather, and holding a vajra in his right hand and a skull cup in his left. A khatvanga, a ritual staff topped with skulls and a trident, rests…

lore.title: The Tenth Day
lore.excerpt: The tenth day of each lunar month, known as Tsechu, is sacred to Guru Rinpoche, and shrines dedicated to him are especially busy on these days, with offerings, ritual feasts known as tsok and the chanting of his mantra. Devotees visit Guru Lhakhangs to pray fo…

lore.title: Documenting Boudha's Smaller Shrines
lore.excerpt: Boudha's smaller shrines and temples, such as this Guru Lhakhang, are often built and maintained by individual communities, families or monasteries, and their histories are rarely documented in published sources. The 2015 earthquake damaged many buildings arou…

monuments.audioHook: In Boudha you will meet one face again and again: a master with a feathered hat, a vajra in one hand and a skull cup in the other, smiling fiercely. He is Guru Rinpoche, Padmasambhava, the lotus-born, who Tibetans say carried Buddhism over the Himalaya in the eighth century after meditating in caves just south of Kathm…
monuments.nepaliSummary: गुरु ल्हाखाङ तिब्बतमा बौद्ध धर्म पुर्‍याउने गुरु पद्मसम्भवलाई समर्पित बौद्धस्थित गुम्बा हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Introduce Padmasambhava and the long link between Nepal and Tibet.

features: community monastery facing the stupa circuit
painted facade with prayer flags and window frames
monuments.disambiguationTip: Use the facade signage and the main altar image to separate the Tamang Gompa from neighbouring monasteries on the kora.

lore.title: The Tamang Community and Boudha
lore.excerpt: The Tamangs are one of Nepal's largest indigenous peoples, living mainly in the hills surrounding the Kathmandu Valley, and most practise a form of Tibetan Buddhism. Their connection with Boudhanath is long and deep: Tamang communities have honoured the stupa …

lore.title: A Community Gompa
lore.excerpt: Community gompas at Boudha typically consist of a prayer hall with a main altar, often on an upper floor, with painted walls and pillars, and rooms for monks and community activities. The facade facing the kora is usually whitewashed or painted, with colourful…

lore.title: Teaching Through Paintings
lore.excerpt: Gompas often display at their entrance a painting of the wheel of life, held in the jaws of Yama, the lord of death. At its centre a pig, a snake and a rooster represent ignorance, aversion and desire, the three poisons that drive the cycle of rebirth. Around …

lore.title: Sonam Lhosar and Community Festivals
lore.excerpt: The Tamang community celebrates Sonam Lhosar, the Tamang New Year, which falls in late winter, with gatherings, music, dances and rituals at gompas and in public spaces across the Kathmandu Valley. Boudha is a natural focus for these celebrations, and the Tama…

lore.title: Community Heritage Around the Stupa
lore.excerpt: Community gompas at Boudha are maintained by their communities, often with limited resources, and they face pressure from urban growth, rising property values and the costs of repair. The 2015 earthquake damaged many buildings in Boudha, and community gompas r…

monuments.audioHook: Not everyone who walks the kora at Boudha is Tibetan. Many are Tamang, one of Nepal's largest indigenous peoples, whose villages ring the hills around the valley and whose grandfathers often carried loads over the Himalaya to Tibet. This is their gompa, a community monastery on the stupa circuit where Tamang monks pray…
monuments.nepaliSummary: तामाङ गुम्बा बौद्ध कोरामा रहेको तामाङ समुदायको गुम्बा हो, जहाँ सोनाम ल्होसारमा विशेष उत्सव हुन्छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Introduce the Tamang community's role at Boudha.

features: monastery near the north-west of the stupa circuit
dharma wheel and deer ornament on the roofline
monuments.disambiguationTip: Check the monastery's name board and main image; several gompas near the north-west kora share similar facades.

lore.title: A Place of Meditation
lore.excerpt: Samten Ling, meaning 'place of meditative concentration' in Tibetan, is the name of a monastery near the Boudhanath circuit. It is sometimes described as one of the older monasteries in Boudha, but Saalik's desk research has not confirmed its founding date, li…

lore.title: Roof Wheels and Golden Deer
lore.excerpt: Tibetan monasteries at Boudha typically display a golden dharma wheel flanked by two deer on the roof above the main entrance, a symbol recalling the Buddha's first sermon in the deer park at Sarnath. The assembly hall, or dukhang, is the heart of the monaster…

lore.title: The Wheel and the Deer
lore.excerpt: The dharma wheel with two deer is one of the most widespread emblems of Buddhism. The wheel, with eight spokes representing the Noble Eightfold Path, symbolises the teaching the Buddha set in motion with his first sermon. The two deer, a male and a female, rec…

lore.title: Daily Assembly and Annual Dances
lore.excerpt: Monastic life at Boudha follows a daily rhythm of assemblies in the prayer hall, where monks chant texts to the sound of drums, cymbals, horns and bells, usually early in the morning and again in the afternoon or evening. Young monks study scriptures, philosop…

lore.title: Monasteries After the Earthquake
lore.excerpt: Many of Boudha's monasteries were damaged in the 2015 earthquake, and their communities undertook repairs and reconstruction, often supported by international networks of followers. Monastery buildings combine reinforced concrete structures, common since the 1…

monuments.audioHook: Look up at the roof of this monastery: a golden wheel with eight spokes, flanked by two golden deer. They recall the deer park in India where the Buddha gave his very first teaching, and you will see them on monasteries all around Boudha. This one is called Samtenling, the place of meditation. Its own story, who founde…
monuments.nepaliSummary: साम्तेनलिङ बौद्धनाथ नजिकैको गुम्बा हो, जसको छानामा धर्मचक्र र दुई सुनौला मृग राखिएका छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Read the dharma wheel and introduce the monastic lineages.

monuments.century: 20th century CE renewal of an older devotional feature
features: continuous ring of brass prayer wheels set into the stupa's base wall
handles polished bright by countless hands
monuments.disambiguationTip: Frame the low wall of brass wheels at the stupa's base; if the dome fills the frame, the match belongs to the stupa record instead.

lore.title: A Ring of Turning Prayers
lore.excerpt: Around the base of Boudhanath, set into niches in the stupa's lower wall, runs a continuous ring of brass prayer wheels, which pilgrims spin as they walk the kora. Prayer wheels became widespread in Tibetan Buddhism as a way for practitioners, literate or not,…

lore.title: Brass, Niches and Rhythm
lore.excerpt: The prayer wheels are cylinders of brass or copper, embossed with mantras and mounted on vertical axles within niches in the stupa's base. Each contains a tightly rolled scroll printed with many repetitions of a mantra. Set side by side, the wheels form a cont…

lore.title: Om Mani Padme Hum
lore.excerpt: The mantra embossed on the prayer wheels, om mani padme hum, is associated with Avalokiteshvara, the bodhisattva of compassion, known in Tibetan as Chenrezig. Often translated loosely as 'the jewel in the lotus', it is understood as invoking compassion and pur…

lore.title: Spinning on the Kora
lore.excerpt: Every day thousands of pilgrims spin the prayer wheels as they circle Boudhanath, many combining the action with recitation of the mantra or with counting beads on a rosary. Elderly Tibetans may walk the kora many times each morning and evening, and the prayer…

lore.title: Wear and Renewal
lore.excerpt: The prayer wheels are among the most heavily used objects in Nepal, turned millions of times each year, and their axles, bearings and handles wear out. They are regularly repaired and replaced by the stupa's caretakers, often with donations from devotees, who …

monuments.audioHook: Reach out your right hand as you walk and spin the brass wheel beside you, then the next, and the next. You are turning prayers. Inside each wheel at the base of Boudhanath is a scroll printed with the mantra om mani padme hum, repeated many times over, and Tibetan Buddhists believe every turn sends those prayers out f…
monuments.nepaliSummary: बौद्धनाथ स्तूपको फेदमा पितलका प्रार्थना चक्रहरूको लहर छ, जसमा ॐ मणि पद्मे हुँ मन्त्र लेखिएको छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Teach the mantra and how to spin the wheels while walking.

features: house on the northern side of the stupa circuit associated with the hereditary custodians
gateway and courtyard facing the stupa
monuments.disambiguationTip: The Chini Lama residence is a house-like building on the north of the kora rather than a temple; confirm it by its gateway and any signage.

lore.title: The Hereditary Custodians of Boudha
lore.excerpt: For more than a century, the Boudhanath stupa was in the custody of a line of hereditary lamas known as the Chini Lamas, or 'Chinese Lamas'. Accounts trace the title to the nineteenth century, when a lama who acted as an intermediary between Nepal and Tibet af…

lore.title: A Custodian's House on the Kora
lore.excerpt: The Chini Lama residence is a house on the circuit around the stupa, with a gateway and courtyard facing the monument. Its architecture is understood to mix Newar, Tibetan and Rana-era influences, with brick walls, whitewashed surfaces, carved woodwork and lat…

lore.title: Authority and Devotion
lore.excerpt: The Chini Lama's role combined religious authority with secular power granted by the state. As custodian, he was responsible for maintaining the stupa, performing rituals and overseeing the offerings of pilgrims, which made the position both influential and we…

lore.title: Stewardship of the Stupa
lore.excerpt: Under the Chini Lamas, the stupa's rituals and festivals were organised and supervised by the custodian's household, including the whitewashing of the dome, the hanging of prayer flags and the reception of pilgrims at Losar and other festivals. Pilgrims from T…

lore.title: Recording a Social History
lore.excerpt: The Chini Lama residence is important less for its architecture than for its place in Boudha's social and political history. Conservation in this case means documenting that history before living memory fades: interviewing descendants and older residents, coll…

monuments.audioHook: On the northern side of the kora stands a house with a long and unusual history. For more than a century, the great stupa of Boudhanath was looked after by a line of hereditary custodians known as the Chini Lamas, the Chinese Lamas. Accounts say the first was a lama who helped negotiate between Nepal and Tibet after a …
monuments.nepaliSummary: चिनियाँ लामा निवास बौद्धनाथ स्तूपको वंशानुगत संरक्षक लामाहरूको घर हो, जसको इतिहास प्रमाणीकरण गर्न बाँकी छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the Chini Lama custodianship story and Boudha's transformation.

features: arched gateway leading from the main road to the stupa plaza
passage beneath a chorten-topped gate that blesses those who walk under it
monuments.disambiguationTip: Frame the gateway arch with the road behind it; the stupa appears through the arch but should not fill the frame.

lore.title: Thresholds to the Stupa
lore.excerpt: Most visitors reach Boudhanath through a gateway from the main road on its southern side, passing from the noise of traffic into the stupa's circular plaza. In Tibetan Buddhist architecture, gateways topped with chortens, known as kani, are built over paths so…

lore.title: The Kani Form
lore.excerpt: A kani is a gateway structure with a passage beneath and a chorten, or stupa form, above or within its roof. Inside the passage, the ceiling is often painted with mandalas, and the walls may carry images of Buddhas, bodhisattvas or protective deities. In Tibet…

lore.title: Blessing Those Who Pass Beneath
lore.excerpt: The chorten above a gateway is a reminder of the Buddha's enlightened mind, and passing beneath it is believed to purify and bless the traveller. The mandala painted on a kani's ceiling places the traveller at the centre of an enlightened universe for the mome…

lore.title: Entering with Intention
lore.excerpt: Pilgrims arriving at Boudha often pause at the gateway, join their palms or touch their foreheads in respect, and then begin the clockwise kora around the stupa. For Tibetan Buddhists, entering a sacred site is an opportunity to set an intention, dedicating th…

lore.title: Recording the Gateways
lore.excerpt: The gateways to Boudhanath have been altered and rebuilt over the decades as the surrounding area urbanised and as the stupa's management developed visitor facilities. The 2015 earthquake affected structures around the stupa, and the gateways were inspected an…

monuments.audioHook: Step through the gateway from the busy road, and the noise seems to fall away as the great white dome of Boudhanath rises in front of you. In Tibetan Buddhist lands, gateways like this are often crowned with a small stupa, called a kani, and anyone who walks beneath it receives a blessing. Some even have mandalas paint…
monuments.nepaliSummary: बौद्धनाथ स्तूपमा पुग्ने प्रवेशद्वारहरूलाई यहाँ अभिलेख गरिएको छ; 'बोन चोर्तेन' नामको अर्थ फिल्ड टोलीले पुष्टि गर्न बाँकी छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Begin at the threshold and explain the blessing of the kani.

features: large white monastery just north of the stupa
gilded roof ornaments above a whitewashed facade
monuments.disambiguationTip: Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling is the large white monastery just north of the stupa; Shechen is further north-east with a red-and-gold facade and a large courtyard.

lore.title: The White Monastery
lore.excerpt: Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling, often called the White Monastery for its whitewashed walls, was founded in 1976 by Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, one of the most respected Tibetan meditation masters of the twentieth century, who settled in Nepal after leaving Tibet. Its name r…

lore.title: A Modern Himalayan Monastery
lore.excerpt: The monastery is a large, multistorey complex built in the Tibetan style with modern materials, its whitewashed walls, painted window frames and gilded roof ornaments rising above the streets north of the stupa. The main assembly hall contains a large image of…

lore.title: Lineages on the Walls
lore.excerpt: The murals of Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling depict the masters of the Kagyu and Nyingma lineages, the Buddhas and bodhisattvas central to their practice, and protective deities. For practitioners these images are not decorations but supports for meditation, showing th…

lore.title: Teachings Open to the World
lore.excerpt: Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling is known internationally for opening its teachings to students from around the world. For many years the monastery has hosted public teachings, and an annual autumn seminar has drawn practitioners from many countries. Its associated insti…

lore.title: Sustaining a Living Institution
lore.excerpt: As a modern monastery, Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling's conservation concerns relate mainly to maintaining its buildings, murals and community. The 2015 earthquake damaged many buildings in Boudha, and monasteries undertook repairs to ensure the safety of their monks a…

monuments.audioHook: Just north of the stupa rises a large white building with golden deer on its roof. This is Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling, the White Monastery, founded in 1976 by Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, a celebrated meditation master who came to Nepal from Tibet. Its name brings together two great Tibetan traditions, Kagyu and Nyingma, and two …
monuments.nepaliSummary: का-न्यिङ शेड्रुप लिङ (सेतो गुम्बा) सन् १९७६ मा तुल्कु उर्ग्येन रिन्पोछेले स्थापना गरेको बौद्धनाथ नजिकैको गुम्बा हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the story of Tibetan exile and the union of lineages.

features: large monastery with a spacious courtyard north-east of the stupa
red, white and gold facade with a grand assembly hall
monuments.disambiguationTip: Shechen is the large red-and-gold monastery with a big courtyard north-east of the stupa; Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling is closer to the stupa and predominantly white.

lore.title: A Monastery Reborn in Exile
lore.excerpt: Shechen Tennyi Dargyeling is the exile seat of Shechen Monastery, one of the great monasteries of the Nyingma school in eastern Tibet, which was destroyed in the 1950s. Its re-establishment at Boudha was led by Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, one of the most revered …

lore.title: A Grand Assembly Hall
lore.excerpt: Shechen is one of the largest monasteries at Boudha, organised around a spacious courtyard where ceremonies and dances take place. Its main assembly hall rises above the courtyard with a red, white and gold facade, gilded roof ornaments and a grand entrance po…

lore.title: Murals of the Nyingma Tradition
lore.excerpt: Shechen's murals and statues present the vision of the Nyingma school, the oldest of the four main schools of Tibetan Buddhism, which traces its teachings to Padmasambhava and the masters of the eighth century. The main hall features a large image of the Buddh…

lore.title: Dances, Drupchen and Daily Prayer
lore.excerpt: Shechen is renowned for its ritual life, including elaborate ceremonies known as drupchen, intensive group practices lasting many days, and for its sacred dances, cham, performed by masked monks in the courtyard. These dances, often held around Losar or on oth…

lore.title: Preserving Arts in Exile
lore.excerpt: Shechen's greatest contribution to heritage conservation lies in preserving the sacred arts and ritual traditions of Tibetan Buddhism, many of which were endangered after the destruction of monasteries in Tibet. The monastery's art school trains painters in tr…

monuments.audioHook: Walk north-east from the stupa to a grand courtyard surrounded by red, white and gold buildings. This is Shechen, a monastery reborn here after its original home in eastern Tibet was destroyed in the 1950s. Its rebuilding at Boudha began in 1980 under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, a master so respected that he taught the Da…
monuments.nepaliSummary: शेचेन तेन्यी दार्गेलिङ सन् १९८० देखि दिल्गो ख्येन्चे रिन्पोछेले बौद्धमा पुनर्स्थापना गरेको ञिङ्मा परम्पराको ठूलो गुम्बा हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: End with the story of sacred arts preserved in exile.

monuments.century: Licchavi origins (site attested by a 464 CE inscription); present temple rebuilt in the early 18th century
features: two-tiered pagoda in a hilltop courtyard surrounded by Licchavi sculptures
four gilded doorways each with a different guardian pair
monuments.disambiguationTip: Changu Narayan is a two-tiered pagoda in a hilltop courtyard full of ancient stone sculptures, with a different pair of guardian animals at each door.

lore.title: The Oldest Temple in the Valley
lore.excerpt: Changu Narayan, crowning a ridge at the eastern edge of the Kathmandu Valley, is widely regarded as the oldest temple site in Nepal still in active worship. A stone pillar in its courtyard bears an inscription of King Manadeva dated 464 CE, the oldest dated in…

lore.title: Four Doors, Four Guardians
lore.excerpt: The temple is a two-tiered Newar pagoda raised on a plinth in the centre of a paved courtyard, its roofs supported by some of the most elaborately carved struts in the valley. Each of its four sides has a gilded doorway framed by repousse panels and toranas, a…

lore.title: Vishnu on the Hill
lore.excerpt: Changu Narayan is dedicated to Vishnu, worshipped here as Narayan and in the form of Garudanarayan, Vishnu riding his eagle-like mount Garuda. The main image inside the sanctum is not shown to the public, but the temple's exterior and courtyard present a rich …

lore.title: Ekadashi and the Hilltop Pilgrimage
lore.excerpt: Changu Narayan is a living temple, and devotees from Bhaktapur, Kathmandu and the surrounding villages come to worship, especially on Ekadashi, the eleventh day of each lunar fortnight, which is sacred to Vishnu. Major festivals include Haribodhini Ekadashi in…

lore.title: After the Earthquake
lore.excerpt: The 2015 earthquake damaged Changu Narayan's main temple and many surrounding structures, cracking walls, displacing struts and toppling some smaller buildings in the courtyard and village. Restoration work, led by the Department of Archaeology with partners, …

monuments.audioHook: Climb to the top of this ridge and you stand at what may be the oldest temple site in Nepal still in daily worship. In the courtyard, a stone pillar carries words carved in the year 464, the oldest dated inscription in the country, proving that Vishnu was honoured here more than fifteen centuries ago. The temple itself…
monuments.nepaliSummary: चाँगुनारायण उपत्यकाको सबैभन्दा पुरानो मानिने विष्णु मन्दिर हो; यहाँको मानदेवको सन् ४६४ को शिलालेख नेपालकै पुरानो मितियुक्त अभिलेख हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Introduce the oldest temple site and its four guardian doors.

features: tall stone pillar inscribed in Licchavi script around its shaft
stands near the western door of the temple
monuments.disambiguationTip: This is a free-standing pillar with Licchavi script carved around its shaft; Kathmandu's Pratap Malla inscription is a slab set into a palace wall.

lore.title: Nepal's Oldest Dated Words
lore.excerpt: The stone pillar standing near the western door of Changu Narayan carries the oldest dated inscription in Nepal, recorded by King Manadeva in 464 CE. Manadeva was one of the most important Licchavi kings, and his inscription is a cornerstone of Nepali history.…

lore.title: A Pillar for Garuda
lore.excerpt: The inscription is carved on the shaft of a tall stone pillar, a garudadhvaja, the type of column erected before Vishnu temples to carry an image of Garuda, Vishnu's mount. The text runs in lines around the shaft in the Licchavi script, a form of Gupta-period …

lore.title: Words as Devotion
lore.excerpt: Although the inscription is primarily a historical record, it is also a devotional act. By dedicating a Garuda standard to Vishnu and recording his deeds on it, Manadeva placed his reign under the god's protection and offered his achievements to him. The story…

lore.title: Honouring the Ancient Pillar
lore.excerpt: The pillar is not a primary focus of worship like the temple's sanctum, but devotees treat it with respect, sometimes touching its base or making small offerings as part of their circuit of the courtyard. Its importance lies more in what it represents: the ant…

lore.title: Protecting a Fifteen-Century Text
lore.excerpt: The Manadeva inscription is one of Nepal's most precious historical documents, and its conservation is a priority. Weathering, pollution and touching have worn the stone surface, and parts of the text are difficult to read. Scholars have relied on careful read…

monuments.audioHook: Look closely at this weathered stone pillar. The lines of old script running around it are the oldest dated words in Nepal, carved for King Manadeva in the year 464. They tell a family story: Manadeva's father had died, and his grieving mother, Queen Rajyavati, wanted to follow her husband in death. Her son begged her …
monuments.nepaliSummary: मानदेवको गरुडध्वज शिलालेख सन् ४६४ मा कुँदिएको नेपालको सबैभन्दा पुरानो मितियुक्त अभिलेख हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell Manadeva and Rajyavati's story at the oldest dated inscription.

features: upright black stone stele carved in deep relief
small figures of worshippers and gods filling the panel
monuments.disambiguationTip: The Vishwaroopa relief shows a many-headed, many-armed Vishnu above a reclining Vishnu; the Trivikrama relief shows a single striding figure.

lore.title: A Licchavi Masterpiece
lore.excerpt: The Vishwaroopa relief at Changu Narayan is one of the masterpieces of Licchavi sculpture, generally dated on stylistic grounds to around the sixth century. It depicts Vishnu in his universal form, as described in the Bhagavad Gita, when Krishna reveals himsel…

lore.title: Carving the Cosmos
lore.excerpt: The relief is carved on an upright stone stele, its surface densely filled with figures. In the upper register, Vishnu appears in his cosmic form, with multiple heads and many arms radiating outward, holding weapons and symbols, surrounded by smaller figures o…

lore.title: Arjuna's Vision
lore.excerpt: In the Bhagavad Gita, before the great battle of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks Krishna to reveal his true form. Krishna grants him divine sight, and Arjuna sees the universe in Krishna's body: all the gods, all beings, the past and the future, blazing w…

lore.title: Worship Beside an Ancient Image
lore.excerpt: The Vishwaroopa relief is part of the living temple complex, and devotees honour it with offerings of flowers, rice and red powder as they circle the courtyard. Its importance is recognised by priests and pilgrims alike, though it is less a focus of daily ritu…

lore.title: Protecting Fragile Stone
lore.excerpt: The Vishwaroopa relief has survived for around fourteen or fifteen centuries, but its surface is vulnerable to weathering, pollution and the accumulation of offerings. The 2015 earthquake shook the Changu courtyard, and the relief was inspected for damage. Con…

monuments.audioHook: Stand before this black stone and look for the many heads and many arms spreading across the top. This is Vishwarupa, Vishnu's universal form, carved by Licchavi sculptors around fourteen centuries ago. It illustrates the moment in the Bhagavad Gita when Krishna reveals to the warrior Arjuna that the whole universe, ev…
monuments.nepaliSummary: विश्वरूप शिला मूर्ति लिच्छविकालीन उत्कृष्ट कलाकृति हो, जसमा विष्णुको ब्रह्माण्डीय रूप र अनन्त नागमाथि सुतेका विष्णु कुँदिएका छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell Arjuna's vision and read both registers of the relief.

features: black stone image of Vishnu seated on Garuda in flight
set within the courtyard near the temple
monuments.disambiguationTip: Garuda Narayan shows Vishnu riding a flying Garuda; Sridhar Vishnu shows Vishnu standing between attendants, and the kneeling Garuda before the western door has no rider.

lore.title: Vishnu in Flight
lore.excerpt: Among the treasures of Changu Narayan's courtyard is a black stone sculpture of Garuda Narayan, Vishnu riding on Garuda, his eagle-like mount, generally attributed on stylistic grounds to the Licchavi period around the sixth century. Changu Narayan itself is o…

lore.title: Carved Movement
lore.excerpt: The sculpture shows Vishnu seated astride Garuda, who spreads his wings as if in flight. Vishnu's multiple arms hold his attributes, and his posture is calm and regal, contrasting with Garuda's dynamic, outstretched form. The stone is dark and polished in plac…

lore.title: The Eagle and the God
lore.excerpt: Garuda is the king of birds, a mythical being with an eagle's head and wings and a human body, who serves as Vishnu's vehicle. In Hindu mythology he is the enemy of serpents, having fought them to obtain the nectar of immortality to win his mother's freedom. H…

lore.title: Honouring Garudanarayan
lore.excerpt: Devotees honour the Garuda Narayan image as part of their worship at Changu, offering flowers, rice and red powder and touching the image or its base. During festivals dedicated to Vishnu, such as Haribodhini Ekadashi, the image receives special attention. Gar…

lore.title: Guarding a Treasure
lore.excerpt: The Garuda Narayan image is among the most valuable sculptures in Nepal, and its protection is a priority. Licchavi sculptures have been targeted by thieves, and several images from the valley were stolen and sold abroad in past decades, though some have since…

monuments.audioHook: Look for the god in flight. In this black stone carving, around fourteen centuries old, Vishnu sits calmly on the back of Garuda, the king of birds, whose wings spread wide as if he has just taken off. Garuda is half eagle and half man, the sworn enemy of serpents, and the fastest servant any god could have. When the w…
monuments.nepaliSummary: गरुडनारायण मूर्तिमा उड्दै गरेका गरुडमाथि विष्णु बसेको दृश्य कुँदिएको छ, जुन लिच्छविकालीन उत्कृष्ट कला मानिन्छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Explain Garuda's mythology and why the temple is called Garudanarayan.

faces the temple's main door
monuments.disambiguationTip: At Changu the royal couple kneel together inside a cage; in Bhaktapur Bhupatindra sits alone on a column, and Patan's Yoganarendra kneels under a cobra hood.

lore.title: A King and Queen in Devotion
lore.excerpt: In the courtyard of Changu Narayan, gilded statues of King Bhupatindra Malla of Bhaktapur and his queen kneel in devotion, facing the temple, enclosed in a protective metal cage. Bhupatindra, who ruled Bhaktapur from 1696 to 1722, was the great builder king wh…

lore.title: Why a Cage?
lore.excerpt: The statues of the king and queen are made of gilt bronze and set on a platform facing the temple, kneeling side by side with their hands joined. Unusually, they are enclosed in a metal cage, which protects them from theft and damage. The cage reflects a sad r…

lore.title: Royal Devotion Before Vishnu
lore.excerpt: The kneeling posture and joined hands of the king and queen express devotion to Vishnu, the deity of Changu Narayan. By placing their images before the temple, the royal couple ensured that their worship would continue forever. Such statues also asserted the k…

lore.title: Remembering the Royal Patrons
lore.excerpt: The royal statues do not receive formal worship like the deities in the courtyard, but they are treated with respect, and visitors often pause to look at them through the cage. Guides use the statues to tell the story of Bhupatindra Malla and his role in shapi…

lore.title: Protection from Theft
lore.excerpt: The cage around the statues is itself a conservation measure, protecting them from theft, a serious threat to Nepal's heritage. In past decades many sculptures and statues were stolen from temples in the valley and sold on international art markets, and effort…

monuments.audioHook: In front of the temple, a king and queen kneel side by side, hands joined in prayer, their gilded bodies glinting behind iron bars. He is Bhupatindra Malla, the builder king of Bhaktapur, who ruled when this temple was rebuilt after a fire in 1702, and beside him is his queen. You may already have met him in Bhaktapur …
monuments.nepaliSummary: चाँगुनारायण मन्दिर अगाडि राजा भूपतीन्द्र मल्ल र रानीका सुनौला सालिक चोरीबाट जोगाउन पिँजडाभित्र राखिएका छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Connect Bhupatindra's two statues and discuss heritage theft.

monuments.century: later Malla centuries CE (attributed on style)
features: two-tiered goddess temple in a corner of the Changu courtyard
smaller than the main temple with carved struts
monuments.disambiguationTip: Chhinnamasta's shrine is a two-tiered goddess temple; Kileshwar is a smaller Shiva shrine with a lingam and a Nandi in front.

lore.title: A Goddess Shrine Beside Vishnu
lore.excerpt: In the courtyard of Changu Narayan stands a two-tiered temple dedicated to Chhinnamasta, one of the ten Mahavidyas, the great wisdom goddesses of Tantric Hinduism. Its precise date has not been established in Saalik's sources, and it is attributed on stylistic…

lore.title: A Two-Tiered Courtyard Temple
lore.excerpt: Chhinnamasta's temple is a two-tiered pagoda in the Newar style, smaller than the main temple, with brick walls, carved wooden doors and struts supporting its roofs. Its struts depict goddesses and Tantric deities, echoing the imagery of the main temple's stru…

lore.title: The Severed-Headed Goddess
lore.excerpt: Chhinnamasta is one of the most startling images in Hindu iconography. She is depicted holding her own severed head in one hand and a sword in the other, with three streams of blood flowing from her neck: one into her own mouth and two into the mouths of her a…

lore.title: Worship of a Fierce Goddess
lore.excerpt: Chhinnamasta is worshipped at Changu by devotees who seek her protection and blessings, with offerings of flowers and red powder and, on certain occasions, animal sacrifices, in keeping with the traditions of Tantric goddess worship. Dashain, the great festiva…

lore.title: Caring for the Courtyard Shrines
lore.excerpt: Chhinnamasta's temple, like other structures in the Changu courtyard, was affected by the 2015 earthquake and required inspection and repair. Its wooden struts and doors are vulnerable to weathering on the exposed hilltop, and its roof must be maintained to ke…

monuments.audioHook: In a corner of the courtyard, a smaller two-roofed temple belongs to one of the most startling goddesses in Hindu tradition: Chhinnamasta, the one who cut off her own head. In her images she holds her severed head in her hand while three streams of blood arc from her neck, feeding herself and two attendants. It sounds …
monuments.nepaliSummary: छिन्नमस्ता देवी मन्दिर चाँगुनारायण परिसरमा रहेको, आफ्नै शिर काटेकी तान्त्रिक देवी छिन्नमस्ताको दुई तले मन्दिर हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Explain Chhinnamasta's iconography and the ten Mahavidyas.

monuments.century: Licchavi or early medieval centuries CE (stylistic dating)
features: black stone stele of a standing Vishnu triad
finely carved crown and jewellery
monuments.disambiguationTip: Sridhar Vishnu stands upright between two attendants; Garuda Narayan shows Vishnu riding a flying Garuda.

lore.title: Vishnu as Sridhar
lore.excerpt: Among the sculptures in Changu Narayan's courtyard is an image of Vishnu in the form known as Sridhar, 'bearer of Shri', the goddess of fortune, shown with Vishnu's consort Lakshmi and his mount Garuda at his side. Sridhar Vishnu images were popular in the Kat…

lore.title: A Triad in Stone
lore.excerpt: The image is carved on a stone stele and shows Vishnu standing upright in the centre, with four arms holding his attributes, flanked by smaller figures of Lakshmi and Garuda. The composition follows a standard arrangement for Vishnu triads in Licchavi and earl…

lore.title: Fortune and Devotion
lore.excerpt: Sridhar Vishnu emphasises the god's relationship with Shri or Lakshmi, the goddess of prosperity, beauty and good fortune. By bearing Shri, Vishnu ensures the well-being of the world and of his devotees. Lakshmi's presence beside him represents the inseparabil…

lore.title: Prayers for Prosperity
lore.excerpt: Devotees honour the Sridhar Vishnu image with offerings of flowers, rice and red powder, and some pray specifically for prosperity and family well-being, in keeping with Vishnu's role as the bearer of fortune. On Ekadashi days and during Vishnu festivals, the …

lore.title: Recording a Courtyard Stele
lore.excerpt: The Sridhar Vishnu stele, like the other stone images at Changu, faces weathering on the exposed hilltop and the effects of offerings, which can accumulate and discolour the stone. The 2015 earthquake shook the courtyard, and images were inspected for cracks a…

monuments.audioHook: Here Vishnu stands calm and upright, four arms holding the conch, discus, mace and lotus, with the goddess of fortune on one side and Garuda, hands folded, on the other. This form is called Sridhar, the bearer of Shri, the goddess of prosperity, and families come to images like this to pray for good fortune and harmony…
monuments.nepaliSummary: श्रीधर विष्णु मूर्तिमा लक्ष्मी र गरुडसहित उभिएका चतुर्भुज विष्णु कुँदिएका छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Compare Sridhar Vishnu with the other Vishnu forms in the courtyard.

features: stone relief of a giant striding figure
small narrative figures at the base
monuments.disambiguationTip: Trivikrama shows one giant striding figure with a leg raised; Vishwaroopa shows many heads and arms, and Narasimha shows a lion-headed figure tearing a demon.

lore.title: Three Steps Across the Universe
lore.excerpt: The Trivikrama relief at Changu Narayan depicts one of the most famous stories of Vishnu: his incarnation as Vamana, a dwarf, who tricked the demon king Bali into granting him as much land as he could cover in three steps, then grew to cosmic size and strode a…

lore.title: Capturing a Cosmic Stride
lore.excerpt: The relief shows Vishnu as Trivikrama with one leg planted on the earth and the other raised high, extending toward the upper edge of the stone to suggest his step across the heavens. His many arms hold his attributes, and his body is shown in a dynamic pose t…

lore.title: Humility and Cosmic Order
lore.excerpt: The story of Vamana and Bali carries several meanings. Bali was a generous and powerful king who had conquered the gods' realms, upsetting the cosmic order. Vishnu, in the humble form of a dwarf, restored balance not through battle but through a request for a …

lore.title: Remembering Vamana
lore.excerpt: The Trivikrama relief is honoured by devotees circling the courtyard, who make offerings and pause to pray. The story of Vamana is remembered in Hindu festivals, and in some traditions a day in the month of Bhadra is dedicated to him as Vamana Dwadashi. At Cha…

lore.title: Weathering on the Hilltop
lore.excerpt: The Trivikrama relief has survived many centuries on the exposed hilltop of Changu, but its surface shows the effects of weathering, and some details have softened. The accumulation of offerings, especially oil and red powder, can damage the stone over time. T…

monuments.audioHook: Find the stone giant with one leg raised high, as if stepping across the sky. This is Trivikrama, Vishnu taking his three cosmic steps. The story goes like this: a powerful demon king named Bali had conquered heaven itself. Vishnu came to him disguised as a humble dwarf and asked for a tiny gift, only as much land as h…
monuments.nepaliSummary: त्रिविक्रम मूर्तिमा वामन अवतारका विष्णुले तीन पाइलामा पृथ्वी, आकाश र स्वर्ग नापेको दृश्य कुँदिएको छ।

lore.title: The Man-Lion of Changu
lore.excerpt: Among the stone images in Changu Narayan's courtyard is a sculpture of Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu, attributed on stylistic grounds to the Licchavi period. Narasimha images were among the most popular Vishnu forms in the Kathmandu Valley, and exam…

lore.title: Ferocity in Stone
lore.excerpt: The Narasimha image shows Vishnu with a lion's head and a human body, with the demon king Hiranyakashipu laid across his knees. His claws tear open the demon's abdomen, a moment of intense violence rendered with controlled skill. The god's multiple arms may ho…

lore.title: Protector of the Devoted
lore.excerpt: The story of Narasimha tells of the demon king Hiranyakashipu, who had obtained a boon that he could not be killed by man or beast, by day or night, inside or outside, on the ground or in the sky, by any weapon. Confident in his invulnerability, he persecuted …

lore.title: Narasimha Jayanti and Protection
lore.excerpt: Narasimha is honoured on Narasimha Jayanti, the anniversary of his appearance, which falls in late spring, and devotees visit his images to pray for protection. At Changu the Narasimha image receives offerings as part of the courtyard circuit, especially durin…

lore.title: Protecting the Courtyard's Avatars
lore.excerpt: The Narasimha image faces the same conservation challenges as other stone sculptures at Changu: weathering on the exposed hilltop, accumulation of offerings and the risk of theft. The 2015 earthquake shook the courtyard, and sculptures were inspected and, wher…

monuments.audioHook: Look for the lion's face. This stone image shows Narasimha, Vishnu as a man-lion, tearing open a demon laid across his lap. The demon king Hiranyakashipu thought he could never die: not by man or beast, not by day or night, not inside or outside, not on the ground or in the sky. So Vishnu burst out of a pillar as a cre…
monuments.nepaliSummary: नरसिंह अवतार ढुङ्गे सालिकमा विष्णुले नरसिंह रूपमा हिरण्यकशिपुलाई काखमा राखी वध गरेको दृश्य छ।

lore.title: Shiva in Vishnu's Courtyard
lore.excerpt: Kileshwar Mahadev is a small temple to Shiva within the courtyard of Changu Narayan. Its name has been explained as referring to Shiva as 'lord of the stake' or 'lord of the nail', a form associated in some traditions with fixing and protecting sacred ground, …

lore.title: A Compact Shiva Pagoda
lore.excerpt: Kileshwar is a compact two-tiered pagoda in the Newar style, with brick walls, a carved wooden doorway and struts supporting its roofs. A Nandi, Shiva's bull, faces the shrine. The temple's small scale allows visitors to see its carvings at close range, and it…

lore.title: The Lingam and the Bull
lore.excerpt: Inside Kileshwar's sanctum is a Shiva lingam, the abstract form of the god, and outside sits Nandi, the bull who is Shiva's vehicle and devoted attendant. The pairing of lingam and Nandi is the most basic sign of a Shiva temple, recognisable to every Hindu dev…

lore.title: Mondays and Shivaratri at Changu
lore.excerpt: Kileshwar receives regular worship from devotees visiting Changu, especially on Mondays, which are sacred to Shiva, and during Maha Shivaratri, when Shiva temples throughout the valley are crowded. Offerings include water, milk, flowers and bel leaves. Because…

lore.title: Small Temples After 2015
lore.excerpt: Kileshwar, like other small temples in the Changu courtyard, was affected by the 2015 earthquake, and its repair formed part of the restoration of the site led by the Department of Archaeology with partners. Small temples are sometimes overlooked in favour of …

monuments.audioHook: Not everything in Changu's courtyard belongs to Vishnu. This compact two-roofed temple, with a stone bull waiting faithfully outside, is Kileshwar Mahadev, a shrine to Shiva. In the Kathmandu Valley the great gods are good neighbours: Vishnu's ancient temple shares its hilltop with Shiva here and with a fierce goddess …
monuments.nepaliSummary: किलेश्वर महादेव चाँगुनारायण परिसरभित्रको नन्दीसहितको सानो दुई तले शिव मन्दिर हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Close the courtyard circuit at Shiva's shrine.

lore.title: A Goddess and a Guru
lore.excerpt: Pharping, a Newar town on the southern rim of the Kathmandu Valley, is one of the most important sacred sites for both Newar and Tibetan Buddhists. On the hillside above the town stands a temple to Vajrayogini, one of the four Vajrayogini shrines traditionally…

lore.title: Temple, Caves and Monasteries
lore.excerpt: The Vajrayogini temple at Pharping is a Newar pagoda with carved struts, gilded elements and a courtyard, set on the hillside above the old town. Around it the hillside holds caves, shrines and newer Tibetan monasteries, creating a layered sacred landscape. Th…

lore.title: The Dakini of Pharping
lore.excerpt: Vajrayogini is a dakini, a female embodiment of enlightened wisdom in Vajrayana Buddhism, typically depicted as red, dancing, holding a curved knife and a skull cup, and wearing ornaments of bone. She represents the transformation of desire and attachment into…

lore.title: Pilgrimage to Pharping
lore.excerpt: Pharping draws pilgrims throughout the year, especially Tibetan Buddhists who come to the caves of Padmasambhava and to the monasteries, and Newar Buddhists and Hindus who honour Vajrayogini. On the tenth day of the lunar month, sacred to Guru Rinpoche, the ca…

lore.title: Balancing Growth and Heritage
lore.excerpt: Pharping has grown rapidly as a pilgrimage centre, with new monasteries, guesthouses and roads changing the landscape around the old town and the Vajrayogini temple. This growth brings income and support for religious institutions, but it also threatens the se…

monuments.audioHook: High on the hillside above Pharping, at the southern edge of the valley, a goddess and a guru share a mountain. The temple here belongs to Vajrayogini, a dancing goddess of Tantric wisdom, one of four believed to guard the Kathmandu Valley. Just a short walk away are small caves where, Tibetans believe, Guru Rinpoche m…
monuments.nepaliSummary: फर्पिङको वज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर गुरु पद्मसम्भवका गुफा नजिकै रहेको, उपत्यकाका चार वज्रयोगिनीमध्ये एक तीर्थस्थल हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Climb from Kali's ravine to the meeting of goddess and guru on one hillside.

lore.title: The Tiger God of a Defiant Town
lore.excerpt: Kirtipur, a Newar town on a ridge south-west of Kathmandu, is famous for its resistance to Prithvi Narayan Shah, the Gorkha king who unified Nepal. Its defenders held out against several assaults in the 1760s before the town finally fell in 1767, and chronicle…

lore.title: A Hilltop Pagoda
lore.excerpt: Bagh Bhairav is a three-tiered pagoda built of brick and timber, with carved struts and a broad facade facing a square in the old town. Its most unusual feature is the collection of swords, shields and other weapons nailed to its walls, which gives the temple …

lore.title: Bhairav as a Tiger
lore.excerpt: Bhairav, the fierce form of Shiva, appears in many guises in the Kathmandu Valley, and at Kirtipur he takes the form of a tiger, bagh in Nepali. A local legend tells of shepherd boys who made a tiger out of clay while grazing their animals and went to find lea…

lore.title: Festivals of a Guardian God
lore.excerpt: Bagh Bhairav is worshipped daily by Kirtipur's residents, and major festivals bring the town together in celebration. Animal sacrifices are offered to the god on certain occasions, in keeping with Bhairav worship in the valley. During the town's festivals, pro…

lore.title: Kirtipur After 2015
lore.excerpt: Kirtipur was affected by the 2015 earthquake, with damage to traditional houses and temples in its old town. Bagh Bhairav required inspection and repair, carried out by local authorities with the community. The town faces pressure from urbanisation, as new bui…

monuments.audioHook: Look at the walls of this temple and you will see old swords and shields hanging there. Kirtipur says they belonged to its defenders. In the 1760s this hilltop town held out against the armies of Prithvi Narayan Shah, the king who would unify Nepal, fighting off attack after attack before finally falling in 1767. The p…

monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the story of the 1767 siege at the town guardian's temple.

monuments.disambiguationTip: Chilanchu is a modest stupa ringed by four small stupas on Kirtipur's southern hill; Swayambhu and Boudha are far larger and busier.

lore.title: Kirtipur's Buddhist Heart
lore.excerpt: Chilanchu Vihar, also called Chilancho, is a Buddhist stupa complex on the southern hill of Kirtipur, dated by inscription to 1515. Kirtipur's population includes a significant Newar Buddhist community, and Chilanchu has long been the centre of their religious…

lore.title: Five Stupas in a Mandala
lore.excerpt: The central stupa of Chilanchu is a hemispherical dome on a base, topped by a harmika and spire, in the classic Newar Buddhist form. Around it four smaller stupas stand at the cardinal directions, reproducing on a small scale the cosmological arrangement of a …

lore.title: The Mandala of the Five Buddhas
lore.excerpt: The arrangement of a central stupa with four smaller stupas reflects the Vajrayana Buddhist mandala of the five Buddhas, each associated with a direction, a colour and an aspect of enlightened wisdom. Vairocana at the centre, Akshobhya in the east, Ratnasambha…

lore.title: Gunla and Community Worship
lore.excerpt: Chilanchu is the focus of Kirtipur's Buddhist rituals, particularly during Gunla, the sacred month of the Newar Buddhist calendar during the monsoon, when devotees visit stupas and monasteries daily, play traditional music and recite texts. Buddha Jayanti, the…

lore.title: Caring for a Community Stupa
lore.excerpt: Chilanchu's conservation depends largely on Kirtipur's Buddhist community, which maintains the stupa and its surroundings through guthis and voluntary contributions. The 2015 earthquake damaged buildings in Kirtipur, including some around the stupa complex, an…

monuments.audioHook: On Kirtipur's southern hill, a white stupa stands in the middle of four smaller ones, like a compass pointing to every direction at once. This is Chilanchu, built in 1515 according to its inscription, and it is the heart of Kirtipur's Buddhist community. The five stupas together form a mandala of the five Buddhas, each…

lore.title: A Temple at the Summit
lore.excerpt: At the highest point of Kirtipur's ridge stands the temple of Uma Maheshwar, dedicated to Shiva and Parvati as the divine couple. It is usually attributed to the seventeenth century, though its exact date has not been confirmed in Saalik's sources. Local accou…

lore.title: Elephants on the Stairs
lore.excerpt: The Uma Maheshwar temple is a three-tiered pagoda raised on a stepped plinth, approached by a stairway guarded by stone elephants. The elephants, described in some accounts as wearing spiked harnesses, give the approach a sense of grandeur. The temple's struts…

lore.title: The Divine Couple on the Hill
lore.excerpt: Uma Maheshwar, Shiva and Parvati together, is one of the most beloved subjects of Newar religious art, representing the harmony of the divine couple on Mount Kailash. The temple's dedication emphasises themes of marital harmony, family well-being and the union…

lore.title: Prayers for Harmony
lore.excerpt: Devotees visit the Uma Maheshwar temple to pray for marital harmony, family well-being and the blessings of the divine couple. Women observe Teej, the festival in which they fast and pray to Parvati for the long life of their husbands or for a good marriage, a…

lore.title: A Hilltop Temple in a Growing City
lore.excerpt: The Uma Maheshwar temple's hilltop position exposes it to weathering and earthquakes, and its reported damage in 1934 shows its vulnerability. The 2015 earthquake affected Kirtipur, and the temple was inspected and repaired as needed. The stone elephants and c…

monuments.audioHook: Climb to the very top of Kirtipur's ridge, past the stone elephants guarding the stairway, and turn around. The whole valley spreads out below you: Kathmandu, Patan and, on a clear day, the white line of the Himalaya. You are at the temple of Uma Maheshwar, Shiva and Parvati together, the divine couple whose mountain h…
