lore.excerpt: Mahabouddha, the 'Temple of a Thousand Buddhas', was built by a Patan family of the Shakya Buddhist community. Tradition credits Abhaya Raj Shakya, a priest who travelled to Bodh Gaya in India, where the Buddha attained enlightenment, and returned determined t…

lore.title: Terracotta Tower in a Courtyard
lore.excerpt: The temple is a tall shikhara, a tapering tower of the north Indian type, built in brick and faced with terracotta tiles, each moulded with a small image of the Buddha. The repetition of thousands of near-identical figures gives the building its popular name a…

lore.title: A Thousand Buddhas
lore.excerpt: Each terracotta tile carries a seated Buddha, most often in the earth-touching gesture, with the right hand reaching down to call the earth to witness his enlightenment. The repetition of the image expresses a Mahayana idea: that there have been countless Budd…

lore.title: Worship in a Neighbourhood Courtyard
lore.excerpt: Mahabouddha is cared for by the Buddhist families of its neighbourhood, who perform daily rituals and maintain the shrine. Lamps are lit, offerings of flowers and rice are made, and on Buddhist festivals the courtyard fills with worshippers. Buddha Jayanti, th…

lore.title: Rebuilt After 1934
lore.excerpt: The great earthquake of 1934 brought Mahabouddha down, and the tower had to be rebuilt almost from scratch. The reconstruction did not perfectly reproduce the original proportions, and attentive visitors notice that the present tower looks slightly different f…

monuments.audioHook: Squeeze through the narrow passage into this courtyard and look up. A tower covered in thousands of tiny Buddhas rises above the rooftops. This is Mahabouddha, the Temple of a Thousand Buddhas, built by a Patan family whose ancestor, legend says, travelled to Bodh Gaya in India, where the Buddha found enlightenment, an…
monuments.nepaliSummary: महाबौद्ध मन्दिर बोधगयाको महाबोधि मन्दिरको नमुनामा बनेको, हजारौं बुद्ध अंकित टेराकोटा इँटाले सजिएको शिखर मन्दिर हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Start with the Bodh Gaya replica and the artisan neighbourhood around it.

features: two-tiered brick pagoda regarded as the oldest in the square
stands at the southern end of the square near the palace
monuments.disambiguationTip: Char Narayan is at the southern end of the square and belongs to Vishnu; Vishwanath has stone elephants at its steps, and Bhimsen has a gilded first-floor balcony.

lore.title: One of Patan's Oldest Temples
lore.excerpt: Char Narayan, also known as Jagannarayan, is often described as the oldest temple standing in Patan Durbar Square, with a construction date usually given as 1565. It is commonly attributed to Purandarasimha, a noble of Patan, at a time when the city was govern…

lore.title: A Classic Two-Tiered Pagoda
lore.excerpt: Char Narayan is a two-tiered brick pagoda raised on a stepped plinth, a compact example of the classic Newar temple form. Its square sanctum has doors on each side, framed by carved wooden panels and toranas, and its two roofs are supported by struts carved wi…

lore.title: Vishnu Facing Every Direction
lore.excerpt: The name Char Narayan means 'four Narayans', usually explained as a reference to Vishnu's presence facing the four directions, protecting the city on every side. The temple's carvings include multi-armed forms of Vishnu bearing his attributes, the conch, discu…

lore.title: Morning Offerings at the Square's Edge
lore.excerpt: Char Narayan receives daily worship, with devotees offering flowers, rice, incense and lamps, especially in the early morning when Patan's residents make their rounds of neighbourhood shrines. Ekadashi, the eleventh day of each lunar fortnight, is sacred to Vi…

lore.title: Restored After 2015
lore.excerpt: Char Narayan was damaged in the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, which shook the temple's brick walls and timber structure. It was among the monuments in Patan Durbar Square whose restoration was carried out with the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust, an organisation…

monuments.audioHook: At the southern end of Patan Durbar Square stands a two-roofed temple that may be the oldest in the square: Char Narayan, built around 1565, decades before Patan's kings raised the stone and gold wonders around it. Its name means four Narayans, Vishnu watching over every direction of the city. Look closely at the roof …
monuments.nepaliSummary: चार नारायण मन्दिर सन् १५६५ तिर बनेको पाटन दरबार क्षेत्रको सबैभन्दा पुरानो मानिने विष्णु मन्दिर हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Compare the early pagoda with the later Malla showpieces of the square.

features: sunken stepped stone bath at the centre of a palace courtyard
stone slab beside the bath said to be the king's bed
monuments.disambiguationTip: Tusha Hiti is enclosed inside the palace's southern courtyard and densely carved with deities; Mani Dhara is a public sunken spout at the square's north end.

lore.title: A King's Private Bath
lore.excerpt: Sundari Chowk is the southern of the three main courtyards of the Patan royal palace, and at its centre lies Tusha Hiti, the king's private bath, completed in 1647 under King Siddhinarasimha Malla. Siddhinarasimha, who also built the Krishna Mandir, was famous…

lore.title: A Sunken Stone Masterpiece
lore.excerpt: Tusha Hiti is a sunken, stepped bath built of finely carved stone, its sides descending to a pool fed by a gilded spout. Water was supplied through the valley's ingenious network of canals and underground channels, the same system that feeds public hitis acros…

lore.title: Goddesses, Bhairavas and Serpents
lore.excerpt: The carvings around Tusha Hiti form a Tantric mandala in stone. Images of the Ashta Matrika, the eight mother goddesses, and of forms of Bhairav line the bath, together with other deities, attendants and nagas, the serpent spirits associated with water. Nagas …

lore.title: Water, Purity and Royal Meditation
lore.excerpt: Water is central to Newar ritual life, and royal baths like Tusha Hiti connected the king's daily purification with the great festivals of the city. Bathing at dawn before worship, especially in the cold months, was considered an act of austerity that generate…

lore.title: Bringing the Courtyard Back
lore.excerpt: Sundari Chowk suffered from long neglect in the twentieth century, and the 2015 earthquake added further damage to its palace wings. The Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust, which has worked extensively in the Patan palace, led a major conservation project in …

monuments.audioHook: Behind these palace walls lies one of the most beautiful baths ever carved in stone. Tusha Hiti, finished in 1647 for King Siddhinarasimha Malla, sinks step by step into the earth, its walls lined with tiny goddesses, Bhairavas and coiled serpents. The king who built the Krishna Mandir outside was famous for his devoti…
monuments.nepaliSummary: सुन्दरी चोकको तुषा हिटी राजा सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले सन् १६४७ मा बनाएको, देवदेवीका ढुङ्गे मूर्तिले सजिएको शाही स्नान कुण्ड हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Introduce royal Tantric ritual through the deities around the bath.

features: large square courtyard with a small gilded shrine at its centre
golden doorway to the Taleju shrine on the southern side
tiered temple roofs rising above the courtyard
monuments.disambiguationTip: Mul Chowk is the large open central courtyard with a small gilded shrine in the middle; Sundari Chowk is the smaller southern court with the sunken stone bath.

lore.title: Heart of the Patan Palace
lore.excerpt: Mul Chowk, the 'main courtyard', is the largest and oldest of the three principal courtyards of the Patan royal palace. In its present form it was completed in 1666 under King Srinivasa Malla, the son of Siddhinarasimha, after earlier phases of building and re…

lore.title: Courtyard of Gilded Doors
lore.excerpt: Mul Chowk is a large square courtyard enclosed by two-storey palace wings with carved windows and doors, a classic Newar quadrangle built on the same principle as a Buddhist monastery. At its centre stands a small gilded shrine, and around its edges rise the t…

lore.title: River Goddesses at the Golden Door
lore.excerpt: The gilt-bronze statues of Ganga and Yamuna that flank the golden door are personifications of India's two holiest rivers, and their presence turns the threshold into a sacred crossing. In Hindu temple architecture, river goddesses at doorways symbolise purifi…

lore.title: Dashain in the Royal Courtyard
lore.excerpt: During Dashain, the great autumn festival of the goddess Durga, Mul Chowk becomes the focus of rituals for Taleju, including animal sacrifices performed by the shrine's priests. These ceremonies continue a royal tradition in which the king's offerings to the g…

lore.title: Restoring the Palace Core
lore.excerpt: Mul Chowk was damaged in the 2015 earthquake, with cracks in its palace wings and damage to temple structures around the courtyard. Conservation work carried out with the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust and the Department of Archaeology aimed to stabilise …

monuments.audioHook: Walk into the heart of the Patan palace, the great courtyard called Mul Chowk, and look for the golden doorway on its southern side. Two goddesses guard it, cast in gilded bronze: Ganga and Yamuna, the holy rivers of India, each standing on her water-animal mount. Pass between them, and tradition says you are purified …
monuments.nepaliSummary: मूल चोक पाटन दरबारको मुख्य चोक हो, जहाँ तलेजु भवानीको मन्दिर र गंगा-यमुनाका सुनौला मूर्ति रहेका छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Connect Taleju worship across the three Malla capitals.

features: large bronze bell hanging between two thick stone pillars
stands in the open square in front of the palace
monuments.disambiguationTip: Patan's bell hangs between two stone pillars; Kathmandu's bell sits in a frame on a raised platform, and Bhaktapur's barking-dog bell stands beside the stone Vatsala Durga temple.

lore.title: A Royal Couple's Bell
lore.excerpt: The Taleju Bell of Patan was erected in 1737 by King Vishnu Malla and his queen, Chandra Lakshmi, during the last decades of Patan's independence. Like the great bells of Kathmandu and Bhaktapur, it was dedicated to Taleju, the royal goddess, and it stood befo…

lore.title: Hanging Between Pillars
lore.excerpt: Unlike Kathmandu's bell, which hangs from a frame on a raised platform, Patan's bell is suspended between two thick stone pillars joined at the top by a beam from which the bell hangs. The arrangement is simple and robust, allowing the heavy bronze to swing fr…

lore.title: Calling the Goddess and the People
lore.excerpt: Bells in Newar religious practice serve several purposes. They announce the start of worship, summon the deity's attention and drive away inauspicious spirits. Patan's great bell performed these roles on behalf of the whole city, its sound linking the palace s…

lore.title: The Bell in Patan's Festivals
lore.excerpt: The bell is rung during the worship of Taleju and on important religious occasions, its deep sound joining the drums and cymbals that accompany Patan's festivals. During Dashain, when Taleju is honoured with special rituals in the palace, and during other majo…

lore.title: Maintaining a Landmark
lore.excerpt: The bell's stone pillars and bronze body are durable, but they require periodic inspection, particularly after earthquakes. The 2015 earthquake shook the entire square and damaged several temples, and the bell's supports were checked for cracks and displacemen…

monuments.audioHook: In front of the Patan palace, a great bronze bell hangs between two stone pillars. King Vishnu Malla and Queen Chandra Lakshmi raised it in 1737 for Taleju, the royal goddess. But Patan tells another story about this bell: citizens with a complaint could ring it, and the king was expected to come out and listen. Imagin…
monuments.nepaliSummary: पाटनको तलेजु घण्ट राजा विष्णु मल्ल र रानी चन्द्रलक्ष्मीले सन् १७३७ मा दुई ढुङ्गे खम्बाबीच झुण्ड्याएका हुन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the grievance-bell tradition and compare the three royal bells.

features: gilt-bronze kneeling king atop a tall stone column
faces the palace and its temples
monuments.disambiguationTip: Patan's king kneels under a cobra hood topped by a bird; Bhaktapur's Bhupatindra Malla sits with folded hands and no cobra canopy.

lore.title: The King Who Might Return
lore.excerpt: The gilt-bronze statue of King Yoganarendra Malla, raised on a tall stone column in front of the Patan palace, dates from the late seventeenth century. Yoganarendra ruled Patan from 1684 until around 1705 and is remembered as a devout king who, according to tr…

lore.title: A Column Crowned with Gold
lore.excerpt: The statue rests on a lotus-shaped throne at the top of a slender stone column several metres high, raising the king far above the crowds in the square. Above him rises the hood of a cobra, a protective canopy, and on the cobra's head perches a small bird. The…

lore.title: Cobra, Bird and Kneeling King
lore.excerpt: The king kneels with his hands joined in prayer, the posture of a devotee before a deity. The cobra hood above him is a symbol of protection drawn from Hindu and Buddhist iconography, recalling the serpent king who sheltered the Buddha and the great serpent on…

lore.title: Keeping Faith with an Absent King
lore.excerpt: The legend of Yoganarendra's possible return has given the statue a unique place in Patan's folklore. Although the practice of keeping a window open for the king is no longer maintained in any formal sense, many residents remember the story, and guides delight…

lore.title: Protecting a Gilded Figure on High
lore.excerpt: The statue's height protects it from handling but exposes it to the weather. Rain, sun and pollution can damage the gilding, and the column must be monitored for stability, especially after earthquakes. The 2015 earthquake shook the square violently, and the c…

monuments.audioHook: Look up at the golden king kneeling high on the stone column in front of the palace. He is Yoganarendra Malla, who ruled Patan more than three centuries ago. Above him rises a cobra's hood, and on top of the cobra sits a tiny bird. That bird holds a promise. Legend says the king left Patan to live as an ascetic, declar…
monuments.nepaliSummary: राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लको सुनौलो सालिक अग्लो ढुङ्गे स्तम्भमा छ; टाउकोमाथि नागको फणा र त्यसमाथि चरा बसेको छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the bird legend and point out the palace windows.

features: stone shikhara rising through twenty-one pinnacles
open pillared pavilions around the lower floors
gilded finial atop the central spire
monuments.disambiguationTip: Krishna Mandir is the only all-stone tower with open pillared galleries in the square; Mahabouddha is terracotta and hidden in a courtyard.

lore.title: A Temple Born of a Dream
lore.excerpt: Krishna Mandir was completed in 1637 by King Siddhinarasimha Malla of Patan, one of the most devout and celebrated rulers of the Malla period. According to legend, Krishna and his consort Radha appeared to the king in a dream, and he built the temple on the sp…

lore.title: Stone Shikhara with Twenty-One Spires
lore.excerpt: Unlike the brick and timber pagodas that dominate the valley, Krishna Mandir is built entirely of stone in the shikhara style of northern India, a tapering tower crowned with a gilded finial. Its design combines this Indian form with Newar inventiveness: the l…

lore.title: Epics Carved in Stone
lore.excerpt: The stone friezes of Krishna Mandir are among the finest examples of narrative carving in Nepal. Along the first floor run scenes from the Mahabharata, the great epic in which Krishna plays a central role, and along the second floor scenes from the Ramayana, t…

lore.title: Krishna Janmashtami
lore.excerpt: Krishna Mandir is the focus of Krishna Janmashtami, the festival of Krishna's birth, held in late summer. On this night thousands of devotees gather in Patan Durbar Square, many staying awake through the night singing devotional songs and offering prayers. Lam…

lore.title: A Stone Temple That Stood Firm
lore.excerpt: Krishna Mandir's stone construction helped it survive the 2015 earthquake with relatively limited damage, while brick and timber temples nearby suffered more severely. Its survival, like its endurance through the 1934 earthquake, has been attributed to the qua…

monuments.audioHook: In 1637 King Siddhinarasimha Malla of Patan had a dream: Krishna and Radha stood before him on this very spot. So he built them a home of stone, unlike anything else in the valley. Look at the tower rising through twenty-one pinnacles, the open pavilions on each level, and the gilded Garuda kneeling on a pillar out fro…
monuments.nepaliSummary: कृष्ण मन्दिर राजा सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले सन् १६३७ मा बनाएको २१ गजुर भएको ढुङ्गे शिखर शैलीको मन्दिर हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Read one Mahabharata panel together and describe Janmashtami night.

features: two-tiered pagoda with heavily carved struts
stone elephants flanking the stairs
monuments.disambiguationTip: Vishwanath has stone elephants on its steps and a Nandi bull opposite; Bhimsen has a gilded balcony above its ground floor.

lore.title: Shiva, Lord of the Universe
lore.excerpt: Vishwanath Mandir, dedicated to Shiva as 'Lord of the Universe', was built in 1627 by King Siddhinarasimha Malla, a decade before he completed the stone Krishna Mandir nearby. The name echoes the famous Vishwanath temple of Varanasi in India, one of Hinduism's…

lore.title: Elephants on the Steps
lore.excerpt: Vishwanath is a two-tiered pagoda raised on a stepped plinth, with heavily carved roof struts and wooden doors. Its most distinctive features are the two stone elephants that guard the front steps, each with a rider, a motif that adds weight and grandeur to th…

lore.title: Guardians and Lingam
lore.excerpt: The stone elephants on Vishwanath's steps are royal symbols, associated with power and protection, and their riders suggest disciplined strength in the service of the god. Elephants also carry associations with Indra, king of the gods, and with prosperity and …

lore.title: Mondays and Shivaratri
lore.excerpt: Vishwanath receives daily worship, with Mondays and the festival of Maha Shivaratri bringing the largest numbers of devotees. On Shivaratri, the great night of Shiva in late winter, Shiva temples throughout the valley are thronged with worshippers, and Patan's…

lore.title: Collapse, Rebuilding and Repair
lore.excerpt: Vishwanath has a long history of damage and repair. Accounts record that part of the temple collapsed in 1990 after heavy monsoon rains weakened its structure, and it was subsequently reconstructed. The 2015 earthquake caused further damage, and the temple req…

monuments.audioHook: Two stone elephants with riders guard the steps of this temple, and across the square a stone bull sits gazing at its door. You are at Vishwanath, the temple of Shiva as Lord of the Universe, built in 1627 by King Siddhinarasimha Malla, the same king who later built the stone Krishna Mandir next door. He borrowed the n…
monuments.nepaliSummary: विश्वनाथ मन्दिर राजा सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले सन् १६२७ मा बनाएको शिव मन्दिर हो, जसको सिँढीमा ढुङ्गाका हात्ती छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Show the sequence from guardians to lingam and the cycle of rebuilding.

features: golden doorway with a gilded window directly above it on the square facade
restored palace courtyard housing bronze sculpture galleries
monuments.disambiguationTip: Look for the gilded doorway with a golden window above it on Patan's palace facade; Bhaktapur's Golden Gate is a free-standing gilded portal set in a whitewashed wall.

lore.title: From Palace Wing to Museum
lore.excerpt: Keshav Narayan Chowk is the northernmost of the main courtyards of the Patan palace. Construction is generally said to have begun in the later seventeenth century and to have been completed in 1734 under King Vishnu Malla, making it the youngest of the palace'…

lore.title: A Golden Door on the Square
lore.excerpt: From the square, the museum is identified by its golden doorway, framed by a gilded torana, with a gilded window directly above it from which the king could appear before his people. Stone lions guard the doorway. Inside, the courtyard follows the classic Newa…

lore.title: Bronzes of the Himalayan World
lore.excerpt: The Patan Museum's collection focuses on the sacred art of the Kathmandu Valley, particularly bronze and gilt-copper images of Hindu and Buddhist deities, many of them made in Patan itself. The galleries explain the iconography of these images, the meaning of …

lore.title: A Museum Within Living Heritage
lore.excerpt: Although the Patan Museum is a secular institution, it sits within a palace that remains part of a living religious landscape. The Keshav Narayan shrine at the centre of the courtyard is still honoured, and the neighbouring Mul Chowk hosts important rituals fo…

lore.title: A Training Ground for Recovery
lore.excerpt: The 1990s restoration of Keshav Narayan Chowk was more than a museum project: it revived traditional building crafts in Patan and trained craftsmen and conservators who would later work on many other monuments. When the 2015 earthquake struck, the museum and p…

monuments.audioHook: See the golden doorway with a gilded window directly above it? From that window, Patan's kings once appeared before their people on festival days. Today the doorway leads into one of the best museums in South Asia, created inside a palace courtyard completed in 1734 and restored in the 1990s with Austrian support. Insi…
monuments.nepaliSummary: पाटन संग्रहालय केशव नारायण चोकमा रहेको छ, जहाँ हिमाली क्षेत्रका धातु र काष्ठ कलाकृति प्रदर्शन गरिन्छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Use the bronzes to teach mudras before continuing to Bhimsen.

monuments.century: late 17th century CE; rebuilt several times
features: three-tiered rectangular pagoda
gilded balcony across the first floor
stands at the northern end of the temple row
monuments.disambiguationTip: Bhimsen is rectangular with a gilded first-floor balcony at the north end of the row; Vishwanath is square with stone elephants on its steps.

lore.title: The Traders' God
lore.excerpt: The temple of Bhimsen stands at the northern end of the temple row in Patan Durbar Square. It is usually dated to the reign of King Srinivasa Malla in the later seventeenth century, although it has been damaged and rebuilt several times, including after a fire…

lore.title: A Rectangular Pagoda with a Golden Balcony
lore.excerpt: Bhimsen's temple differs from the square pagodas around it. It is rectangular in plan and rises in three tiers, with a richly gilded balcony projecting across the first floor. The shrine is located on the upper floor, a feature typical of Bhimsen temples, whil…

lore.title: Strength in Service of Commerce
lore.excerpt: Bhimsen is depicted as a powerful figure, often holding a mace, the weapon he wields in the Mahabharata. His reputation for strength and loyalty made him an ideal protector for traders who undertook long, dangerous journeys across Himalayan passes to Tibet. Ne…

lore.title: Merchants' Offerings
lore.excerpt: Bhimsen's temple receives regular worship from traders, shopkeepers and families seeking prosperity. Many merchants visit before beginning new business ventures or important journeys, offering flowers, coins and other gifts. The temple is particularly busy on …

lore.title: Repeated Rebuilding
lore.excerpt: Few temples in the square have been rebuilt as often as Bhimsen. After a fire in the late seventeenth century it was restored, and after the 1934 earthquake it was substantially rebuilt. Accounts also record a major renovation in 1967, and the 2015 earthquake …

monuments.audioHook: At the north end of the temple row, a three-tiered temple flashes with a golden balcony. This is the home of Bhimsen, the mighty hero of the Mahabharata, who in Nepal became the god of traders. For centuries Patan's merchants walked for weeks over Himalayan passes to trade with Tibet, and before they left, they came he…
monuments.nepaliSummary: भीमसेन मन्दिर व्यापारीहरूका संरक्षक देवता भीमसेनको तीन तले मन्दिर हो, जसको पहिलो तलामा सुनौलो बार्दली छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Connect Bhimsen worship to the Newar trade with Tibet.

features: small shrine with a carved stone Uma Maheshwar stele seen through the doorway
Ganesh and Kumar among the attendant figures
monuments.disambiguationTip: Patan's Uma Maheshwar is a small shrine with a stone stele of the couple inside; Kathmandu's Shiva Parvati temple shows painted wooden figures at an upper window, and Kirtipur's Uma Maheshwar is a hilltop pagoda.

lore.title: A Thousand Years of the Divine Couple
lore.excerpt: Images of Uma Maheshwar, Shiva seated with his consort Parvati, are among the most beloved subjects of Kathmandu Valley sculpture, and Patan is especially rich in them. The earliest surviving examples date from the Licchavi period, more than a thousand years a…

lore.title: Reading an Uma Maheshwar Stele
lore.excerpt: Uma Maheshwar images in Patan typically take the form of a carved stone stele, set into a shrine or niche, in which the divine couple is shown on a stylised Mount Kailash. Shiva sits at ease, one leg folded and the other pendant, while Parvati sits on his left…

lore.title: Shiva, Parvati and Their Household
lore.excerpt: The Uma Maheshwar composition is a portrait of a divine family. Shiva is recognisable by his matted hair, crescent moon and trident, and Parvati, also called Uma, by her jewellery and gentle posture, often with one arm around Shiva's shoulder. Below them stand…

lore.title: Blessings for Marriage and Family
lore.excerpt: Uma Maheshwar shrines are visited by couples and families seeking blessings for marriage, harmony and children. Women in particular honour the divine couple during Teej, the late-summer festival in which they fast and pray to Parvati for the long life of their…

lore.title: Caring for Stone Under Offerings
lore.excerpt: Stone steles like those of Uma Maheshwar are durable, but centuries of offerings take their toll. Layers of red powder, oil, rice and flowers can accumulate on the surface, hiding the carving and trapping moisture that encourages biological growth. Conservator…

monuments.audioHook: Look through the doorway of this small shrine and you may find a scene of quiet affection carved in stone: Shiva sitting at ease on Mount Kailash, with Parvati leaning against him, their sons and animals gathered around. This is Uma Maheshwar, the divine couple, and Patan has honoured them in stone for over a thousand …
monuments.nepaliSummary: उमा महेश्वरका मूर्तिमा कैलाश पर्वतमा शिव र पार्वती सँगै बसेको दृश्य कुँदिएको हुन्छ; पाटनमा यस्ता मूर्ति हजार वर्षदेखि पुजिँदै आएका छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Read the Uma Maheshwar family scene and discuss image theft and return.

features: sunken stepped stone pit with carved spouts
Mani Mandap pavilions on platforms beside it
monuments.disambiguationTip: Mani Dhara is a public sunken water spout at the square's north end with pavilions beside it; Tusha Hiti is enclosed inside the palace.

lore.title: One of the Valley's Oldest Water Spouts
lore.excerpt: Manga Hiti, also known as Mani Dhara, is a sunken stone water spout at the northern end of Patan Durbar Square and one of the oldest functioning hitis in the Kathmandu Valley. It is commonly dated to around 570 CE, in the Licchavi period, when kings and nobles…

lore.title: Engineering a Sunken Spout
lore.excerpt: Manga Hiti is built in a stepped pit below street level, allowing water from underground channels to flow by gravity through carved stone spouts. The pit's walls are faced with stone and brick, and steps lead down from the square so that people can collect wat…

lore.title: Makaras, Nagas and the Sacredness of Water
lore.excerpt: The carved makaras on Manga Hiti's spouts are guardians of water in South Asian iconography, associated with rivers, fertility and abundance. The water that flows from their mouths is regarded as purified and blessed. Small shrines and images set into the pit …

lore.title: Water for Daily Life and Festivals
lore.excerpt: For centuries, Manga Hiti supplied water to the residents of central Patan for drinking, washing and ritual purification. Women and children came at dawn to fill their water jars, and the spout was a place of daily meeting and conversation. During festivals th…

lore.title: Keeping Ancient Water Flowing
lore.excerpt: Manga Hiti's survival as a functioning spout depends on the health of the underground channels and ponds that feed it, many of which have been damaged or disrupted by urban development, groundwater extraction and changes in land use. When channels are blocked …

monuments.audioHook: Walk down the stone steps into this sunken pit, and listen for the sound of water. You are at Manga Hiti, also called Mani Dhara, one of the oldest working water spouts in the valley, traditionally dated to around 570 in the Licchavi period. The water comes from hidden channels that ancient engineers dug to carry rain …
monuments.nepaliSummary: मंगा हिटी (मणिधारा) लिच्छविकालमा बनेको मानिने उपत्यकाकै पुरानो ढुङ्गेधारा मध्ये एक हो, जुन अझै पनि चलिरहेको छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Explain Licchavi water engineering and the community revival of hitis.

monuments.century: 12th century CE by tradition; rebuilt and embellished in later centuries
features: three-tiered gilded copper roof over the main shrine
courtyard crowded with bells, lamps and donated images
turtles roaming the courtyard
monuments.disambiguationTip: The Golden Temple is a courtyard monastery whose main shrine has gilded roofs and facade; Mahabouddha is a terracotta tower with no gilded courtyard.

lore.title: A Monastery of Golden Colour
lore.excerpt: Hiranya Varna Mahavihar, the 'golden-coloured great monastery', is better known as Kwa Bahal or simply the Golden Temple. It is one of the most important Buddhist monasteries in Patan, and tradition attributes its founding to King Bhaskaradeva in the twelfth c…

lore.title: Gilded Facade and Courtyard
lore.excerpt: Kwa Bahal is entered through a doorway guarded by lions, leading into a rectangular courtyard surrounded by two-storey buildings. Facing the entrance is the main shrine, whose facade is covered with gilded repousse panels and crowned with a three-tiered gilded…

lore.title: Shakyamuni and the Child Priest
lore.excerpt: The main shrine houses an image of Shakyamuni Buddha, the historical Buddha, and the courtyard contains many images of Buddhas, bodhisattvas and protective deities. One of Kwa Bahal's most remarkable traditions is the role of the child priest: a boy from the s…

lore.title: Daily Worship and the Buddhist Calendar
lore.excerpt: Kwa Bahal's courtyard is alive with daily worship from dawn, as members of the sangha and devotees light lamps, ring bells and make offerings. The month of Gunla, during the monsoon, is a particularly important time, when Newar Buddhists visit monasteries and …

lore.title: Maintaining a Living Monastery
lore.excerpt: Kwa Bahal's conservation is the responsibility of its sangha, who have maintained the monastery for centuries through donations and collective effort. The gilded metalwork requires periodic regilding and cleaning, and the brick and timber buildings must be rep…

monuments.audioHook: Take off anything made of leather, step past the lions, and enter a courtyard where almost every surface gleams with gold. This is Kwa Bahal, the Golden Temple of Patan, a Buddhist monastery whose founding tradition goes back to the twelfth century. Look at the main shrine: its facade and three roofs are covered in gil…
monuments.nepaliSummary: हिरण्यवर्ण महाविहार (क्वा बहाल) पाटनको सुनौलो छाना भएको प्रसिद्ध बौद्ध विहार हो, जहाँ बालक पुजारीले एक महिनासम्म पूजा गर्छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Introduce the sangha system and the child priest tradition.

monuments.century: 14th century CE; upper tiers added later
features: five-tiered pagoda, one of only two free-standing five-roofed temples in the valley
sacred pond in the courtyard believed to be fed from Gosainkunda lake
monuments.disambiguationTip: Kumbheshwar is a five-roofed temple in Patan's northern neighbourhood beside a sacred pond; Nyatapola in Bhaktapur stands on a tall stepped plinth lined with paired guardian statues.

lore.title: Patan's Five-Roofed Temple
lore.excerpt: Kumbheshwar is one of the oldest temples in Patan and one of only two free-standing five-roofed pagodas in the Kathmandu Valley, the other being Nyatapola in Bhaktapur. According to the chronicles, it was founded in 1392 by King Jayasthiti Malla, the ruler who…

lore.title: Five Roofs Over a Neighbourhood
lore.excerpt: Kumbheshwar's five roofs rise in diminishing tiers above a square brick sanctum, creating a tall, slender silhouette that dominates the surrounding neighbourhood. Each roof is supported by carved wooden struts depicting deities, and the eaves are hung with bel…

lore.title: Shiva of the Sacred Water Pot
lore.excerpt: The name Kumbheshwar comes from kumbha, a water pot, and the temple's lingam is associated with the sacred water of its courtyard pond. Legend holds that the pond is connected by an underground channel to Gosainkunda, the holy lake high in the Himalayas north …

lore.title: Janai Purnima
lore.excerpt: Kumbheshwar's greatest festival is Janai Purnima, the full moon of the monsoon month of Shrawan, when Hindu men renew the sacred thread worn across the chest and devotees tie protective threads around their wrists. On this day thousands of pilgrims who cannot …

lore.title: Repairing the Upper Tiers
lore.excerpt: Tall temples like Kumbheshwar are especially vulnerable to earthquakes, as the upper tiers experience greater movement during shaking. In the 2015 earthquake the temple's uppermost tier was damaged, and its restoration became an important project in Patan's re…

monuments.audioHook: Five roofs, one above the other, rise over this Patan neighbourhood. Only two free-standing temples in the whole valley have five, and this is the older one: Kumbheshwar, founded in 1392, centuries before the famous Nyatapola in Bhaktapur. Now look at the pond in the courtyard. Legend says its water flows underground f…
monuments.nepaliSummary: कुम्भेश्वर मन्दिर सन् १३९२ मा स्थापना भएको पाँच तले शिव मन्दिर हो; यसको पोखरी गोसाइँकुण्डसँग जोडिएको जनविश्वास छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Share the Gosainkunda legend at the five-roofed temple before turning south.

features: three-tiered pagoda in the temple row of Patan Durbar Square
bright new timber from its post-2015 reconstruction
monuments.disambiguationTip: Hari Shankar has three roofs and fresh rebuilt timber; Vishwanath has two roofs and stone elephants, and Char Narayan has two roofs at the square's southern end.

lore.title: A Princess's Temple to Two Gods
lore.excerpt: The Hari Shankar temple in Patan Durbar Square is dedicated to Hari Shankar, a combined form of Vishnu, known as Hari, and Shiva, known as Shankar. It is usually attributed to the early eighteenth century and to Yogamati, a daughter of King Yoganarendra Malla,…

lore.title: Three Roofs Rebuilt
lore.excerpt: Hari Shankar is a three-tiered Newar pagoda raised on a stepped plinth, with carved roof struts, wooden doors and stone lions on its steps. Its proportions follow the classic form of the square's larger temples, rising in three diminishing roofs crowned by a g…

lore.title: Vishnu and Shiva United
lore.excerpt: Hari Shankar, also called Harihara, represents the union of Vishnu and Shiva in a single deity, typically shown with one half of the body bearing Vishnu's attributes and the other half Shiva's. The image expresses the idea that the preserver and the destroyer …

lore.title: Worship in the Temple Row
lore.excerpt: Hari Shankar receives daily worship from Patan's residents, who include it in their morning rounds of the square's temples. Devotees of both Vishnu and Shiva honour the combined deity, and festivals of both gods bring worshippers, including Ekadashi days sacre…

lore.title: A Showcase of Post-2015 Rebuilding
lore.excerpt: The reconstruction of Hari Shankar after its collapse in 2015 is one of the best-documented heritage recovery projects in Patan. The Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust, working with the Department of Archaeology and the community, recorded the fallen elements…

monuments.audioHook: This three-roofed temple looks brand new, and in a way it is. Hari Shankar collapsed completely in the 2015 earthquake, and craftsmen rebuilt it piece by piece, rescuing old carvings from the rubble and carving new ones by hand. The temple honours Hari Shankar, a single god who is half Vishnu and half Shiva, proof that…
monuments.nepaliSummary: हरिशंकर मन्दिर विष्णु र शिवको संयुक्त रूपलाई समर्पित तीन तले मन्दिर हो, जुन २०१५ को भूकम्पपछि पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Return to the square to see a temple rebuilt after 2015 and the half-Vishnu, half-Shiva god.

monuments.century: early foundation by tradition; present buildings of the Malla and later centuries
features: monastery courtyard crowded with metal statues of animals
stucco-faced shrine building facing the courtyard
monuments.disambiguationTip: Uku Bahal's courtyard is crowded with free-standing metal animals in south Patan; Kwa Bahal, the Golden Temple, is north of the square and its shrine facade is covered in gilded panels.

lore.title: One of Patan's Oldest Monasteries
lore.excerpt: Rudra Varna Mahavihar, known locally as Uku Bahal, is regarded as one of the oldest Buddhist monasteries in Patan, located a short walk south of Durbar Square near Mahabouddha. Tradition attributes an early foundation to the site, and the monastery is said to …

lore.title: A Courtyard of Metal Animals
lore.excerpt: Uku Bahal's courtyard is famous for the dense collection of metal and stone figures that fill its open space: elephants, lions, peacocks, garudas and other creatures, along with statues of donors and royal figures, many mounted on pedestals and some protected …

lore.title: Guardians and Donors
lore.excerpt: The animals in Uku Bahal's courtyard carry layered meanings. Elephants and lions are royal symbols of strength and protection, peacocks evoke beauty and the transformation of poison into wisdom, and garudas recall the swift power of the enlightened mind. Many …

lore.title: Daily Rituals of the Sangha
lore.excerpt: Uku Bahal remains an active monastery, with daily rituals performed by members of its sangha, who light lamps, make offerings and maintain the shrine. During the Newar Buddhist month of Gunla, devotees visit the monastery regularly, playing traditional music a…

lore.title: Protecting a Sculpture Courtyard
lore.excerpt: Uku Bahal's open courtyard full of metal sculpture makes it particularly vulnerable to theft, and in past decades valuable images have been stolen from monasteries across the valley. Railings and supervision help to protect the figures, but detailed documentat…

monuments.audioHook: Step into this quiet courtyard south of Durbar Square and you will find yourself surrounded by a menagerie of metal: elephants, lions, peacocks and garudas, standing on pedestals among statues of kneeling donors. This is Uku Bahal, the Rudra Varna Mahavihar, regarded as one of the oldest Buddhist monasteries in Patan. …
monuments.nepaliSummary: रुद्रवर्ण महाविहार (उकु बहाल) पाटनको पुरानो बौद्ध विहार हो, जसको चोकमा धातुका हात्ती, सिंह, मयूर र गरुडका मूर्ति छन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: End the loop near the start among the metal animals of a lesser-known monastery.

monuments.century: 5th century CE by chronicle tradition; legendary origins far older
features: white hemispherical dome topped by a gilded square harmika with painted eyes
thirteen gilded rings forming the spire
hilltop platform crowded with chaityas and shrines
monuments.disambiguationTip: Swayambhu's stupa is smaller and crowded with shrines on a hilltop; Boudhanath's stupa sits on a vast tiered mandala platform on flat ground.

lore.title: A Stupa Older Than Memory
lore.excerpt: Swayambhu Mahachaitya crowns a hill west of Kathmandu and is one of the oldest and most sacred Buddhist monuments in Nepal. Chronicles credit an early Licchavi king, Vrishadeva, with building or enlarging the stupa in the fifth century, and Licchavi-period rec…

lore.title: Dome, Eyes and Spire
lore.excerpt: The stupa follows a classic plan rich in symbolism. A white hemispherical dome rises from a circular base, representing the womb of the universe. Above it sits the harmika, a square block painted on all four sides with the eyes of the Buddha, and above that a …

lore.title: The All-Seeing Eyes
lore.excerpt: The eyes painted on the harmika are among the most recognisable images in Nepal. They represent the all-seeing wisdom and compassion of the Buddha, gazing in every direction over the valley. Below and between the eyes, a curling sign resembling a question mark…

lore.title: Circling the Stupa at Dawn
lore.excerpt: Every morning before sunrise, devotees climb Swayambhu's hill to circle the stupa clockwise, spinning prayer wheels, lighting butter lamps and chanting. Newar Buddhists from Kathmandu, Tibetan monks and lay pilgrims, and Hindus who honour the stupa as sacred a…

lore.title: Regilded, Then Shaken in 2015
lore.excerpt: Swayambhu has been repaired many times. Between 2008 and 2010 the stupa's upper parts were renovated and regilded with gold donated through the Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center, an international Buddhist organisation, in a project that also drew on traditiona…

monuments.audioHook: Climb the last of the steep stone steps and look up into the eyes. Painted on all four sides of the golden tower, the eyes of the Buddha gaze across the whole Kathmandu Valley, and the curl beneath them is the Nepali number one, for unity. Legend says this valley was once a lake, and a lotus rose from the water bearing…
monuments.nepaliSummary: स्वयम्भू महाचैत्य काठमाडौंको पश्चिमी डाँडामा रहेको, बुद्धका आँखा कोरिएको उपत्यकाकै पुरानो र पवित्र स्तूप हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: Teach the stupa's symbolism from base to parasol.

features: small gilded pagoda immediately beside the stupa
constant stream of families making offerings at the doorway
monuments.disambiguationTip: Swayambhu's Harati temple stands right beside the stupa on the hilltop; Boudha's Ajima shrine is a small pagoda on the flat stupa circuit.

lore.title: From Ogress to Protector
lore.excerpt: Beside the great stupa stands a small gilded pagoda dedicated to Harati, known to Newars as Ajima, 'grandmother'. Buddhist legend tells that Hariti was once an ogress who devoured other people's children. The Buddha hid one of her own five hundred children, an…

lore.title: A Gilded Shrine Beside the Stupa
lore.excerpt: The Harati temple is a compact pagoda with gilded roofs and a richly decorated facade, set on the hilltop platform close to the main stupa. Its gilded metal roofs and toranas glow against the white dome of the stupa and the colourful prayer flags. The temple's…

lore.title: The Goddess and Her Children
lore.excerpt: Harati is depicted as a mother goddess holding or surrounded by children, a gentle image that contrasts with the fierce ogress of her legend. In Buddhist teaching her story illustrates the transforming power of compassion: even a being who has caused great suf…

lore.title: Mothers, Children and Offerings
lore.excerpt: Harati's temple is busy throughout the day with mothers, grandmothers and families bringing children for blessings. Offerings of rice, flowers, red powder, eggs, sweets and coins are made, and many devotees ring the temple's bells as they arrive. When a child …

lore.title: Caring for a Busy Shrine
lore.excerpt: The Harati temple's constant use creates conservation challenges. Smoke from lamps and incense blackens surfaces, offerings accumulate, and the movement of crowds wears the floors and steps. The gilded roofs and metalwork require periodic cleaning and regildin…

monuments.audioHook: Beside the great stupa, families crowd around a small golden temple, holding up their children for blessings. This is the shrine of Harati, whom Newars call Ajima, grandmother. Her story is surprising. Buddhist legend says she was once an ogress who ate other people's children, until the Buddha hid one of her own. Mad …
monuments.nepaliSummary: हारती (अजिमा) बालबालिकाको रक्षक देवी हुन्; स्वयम्भू स्तूपको छेउको सुनौलो मन्दिरमा परिवारहरू बच्चाको आशीर्वाद लिन आउँछन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the ogress-to-protector story and point out offerings made for children.

features: huge gilded thunderbolt at the head of the eastern stairway
flanked by two white shikhara towers
monuments.disambiguationTip: The Vajra Dhatu Mandala is the giant gilded thunderbolt lying on a round pedestal at the head of the stairs; the white towers either side are Pratappur and Anantapur.

lore.title: A King's Thunderbolt
lore.excerpt: At the top of Swayambhu's eastern stairway lies an enormous gilded vajra, the ritual thunderbolt of Vajrayana Buddhism, resting on a circular stone pedestal carved as a mandala. It is usually said to have been offered by King Pratap Malla of Kathmandu in 1667,…

lore.title: Gilded Metal on a Mandala Drum
lore.excerpt: The vajra is made of gilded copper and lies horizontally on a round stone pedestal, its two ends shaped like closed lotuses with prongs curving toward a central point. The pedestal is carved with a mandala representing the Dharmadhatu, the realm of ultimate re…

lore.title: Indestructible Wisdom
lore.excerpt: The vajra, called dorje in Tibetan, is the central symbol of Vajrayana Buddhism, the form of Buddhism practised by Newar Buddhists and in Tibet. It represents the indestructible nature of the enlightened mind, as hard as diamond and as powerful as a thunderbol…

lore.title: Touching the Vajra
lore.excerpt: Pilgrims who reach the top of the eastern stairway usually begin their visit at the vajra, touching it with their foreheads or hands, offering flowers and coins and circling it clockwise. Many then proceed to circle the stupa itself. During major festivals suc…

lore.title: Weathering at the Summit
lore.excerpt: Exposed on the hilltop, the vajra and its pedestal face sun, rain and the constant touch of pilgrims. Gilding wears away where hands rest most often, and the stone pedestal can weather and crack, softening the carved mandala and animals. The 2015 earthquake da…

monuments.audioHook: At the top of the stairs, before you even see the stupa properly, you meet a giant golden thunderbolt lying on a round stone drum. This is the great vajra of Swayambhu, offered, it is said, by King Pratap Malla in 1667. In Vajrayana Buddhism the vajra stands for wisdom that cannot be destroyed, as hard as diamond and a…
monuments.nepaliSummary: वज्रधातु मण्डलमा राजा प्रताप मल्लले चढाएको भनिएको सुनौलो विशाल वज्र ढुङ्गाको मण्डलमाथि राखिएको छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Introduce Vajrayana symbolism at the threshold of the stupa.

features: matching pair of white shikhara towers flanking the great vajra
gilded finials and small bells at their summits
monuments.disambiguationTip: Pratappur and Anantapur are a matching pair of white plastered towers beside the vajra; Bhaktapur's Vatsala Durga is a single grey-stone shikhara.

lore.title: A King's Twin Towers
lore.excerpt: The two white shikhara towers that flank the great vajra at the top of Swayambhu's eastern stairway are known as Pratappur and Anantapur. Tradition attributes them to King Pratap Malla of Kathmandu in the mid-seventeenth century, with Anantapur sometimes assoc…

lore.title: Shikharas in White
lore.excerpt: Pratappur and Anantapur are shikhara towers, built in brick and coated in white plaster, each tapering to a gilded finial. Their form reflects the influence of north Indian temple architecture, which had become fashionable in the valley, as seen in Patan's Kri…

lore.title: Guardians of the Threshold
lore.excerpt: The towers house shrines to Tantric Buddhist deities, protectors associated with the esoteric practices of Vajrayana. Their images are not displayed publicly, in keeping with the Newar tradition of reserving powerful Tantric deities for initiates. As a pair fl…

lore.title: Passing Between the Towers
lore.excerpt: Pilgrims arriving at the top of the eastern stairway pass between the twin towers and the vajra on their way to the stupa. Many pause to touch the vajra and bow toward the towers before beginning their circumambulation. Because the shrines inside are reserved …

lore.title: Damage and Repair After 2015
lore.excerpt: The 2015 earthquake damaged the twin shikharas, with Pratappur suffering serious damage to its upper structure. Slender towers of brick and plaster are vulnerable to earthquakes, as their height amplifies shaking, and they had been damaged in earlier events to…

monuments.audioHook: As you step off the last stair at Swayambhu, two white towers stand on either side of you like gatekeepers. They are Pratappur and Anantapur, raised in the seventeenth century by King Pratap Malla, and tradition links one to the king and the other to his queen. Their tall, tapering shape comes from Hindu temples of the…
monuments.nepaliSummary: प्रतापपुर र अनन्तपुर स्वयम्भूको पूर्वी सिँढीको टुप्पोमा वज्रका दुवैतिर रहेका सेता शिखर मन्दिर हुन्।
monuments.talkingPoint: Explain the Hindu form, Buddhist content and the 2015 damage.

features: small pond at the foot of the hill with a standing Buddha at its centre
railings lined with people tossing coins toward a pot
monuments.disambiguationTip: The World Peace Pond is small, with a standing Buddha in the middle; Bhaktapur's Siddha Pokhari is a large historic reservoir with no central statue.

lore.title: A Modern Pond at an Ancient Hill
lore.excerpt: The World Peace Pond lies near the foot of Swayambhu hill, along one of the approaches to the stupa. Unlike the ancient monuments on the summit, it is a modern addition, created in the later twentieth century as part of efforts to beautify the surroundings of …

lore.title: Water and a Standing Buddha
lore.excerpt: The pond is a small, stone-edged basin with a standing image of the Buddha in its centre, rising from the water on a pedestal. A small vessel set in the water serves as a target for visitors who toss coins, hoping to land them inside for good luck. Walkways an…

lore.title: The Buddha as Teacher of Peace
lore.excerpt: The standing Buddha in the pond is shown with a raised hand, a posture associated with the abhaya mudra, which means 'do not fear'. Standing images of the Buddha often represent him in his role as a teacher walking among people, and the placement in water evok…

lore.title: Coins, Wishes and Rest
lore.excerpt: The most visible ritual at the World Peace Pond is the tossing of coins toward the vessel in the water. Visitors, both Nepali and foreign, try their luck, and success is believed to bring good fortune or the fulfilment of a wish. Some pilgrims also bow or offe…

lore.title: Maintaining a Modern Feature
lore.excerpt: As a modern structure, the World Peace Pond faces different conservation issues from the ancient monuments on the hill. Water quality, algae, litter and the maintenance of concrete and paving are the main concerns. Coins thrown into the pond must be collected …

monuments.audioHook: Before you climb Swayambhu's hill, stop at this small pond where a standing Buddha rises from the water. Nepalis and visitors alike take a coin, take aim, and try to land it in the little pot in the water for good luck. Unlike the ancient stupa above you, the World Peace Pond is a modern addition, created to welcome pi…
monuments.nepaliSummary: विश्व शान्ति पोखरी स्वयम्भू डाँडाको फेदमा रहेको, बीचमा उभिएका बुद्धको मूर्ति भएको आधुनिक पोखरी हो।
monuments.talkingPoint: End the circuit at the coin pond after descending the western side.

monuments.century: 17th century CE inscription; shrine tradition older
features: plain shrine building on the north-west of the hilltop platform
sealed inner chambers said to hold the meditating master Shantikar
monuments.disambiguationTip: Shantipur is a closed shrine building with painted Tantric guardians at its door on the north-west of the platform; Harati is a gilded pagoda right beside the stupa.

lore.title: The Master Who Never Left
lore.excerpt: Shantipur, on the north-western side of Swayambhu's hilltop, is one of the most mysterious shrines in the valley. It is one of the five 'pura' shrines of Swayambhu associated with the elements, Shantipur representing the sky or space. According to the Swayambh…

lore.title: A Closed Shrine Building
lore.excerpt: Shantipur is a modest building on the hilltop platform, with a doorway guarded by painted images of Tantric protective deities. Its exterior is plain compared with the gilded shrines nearby, but its significance lies in what is hidden: the series of undergroun…

lore.title: Painted Guardians and Hidden Mandalas
lore.excerpt: The painted deities at Shantipur's entrance are fierce protectors who guard the sacred chamber from intruders. Their wrathful expressions, flaming halos and weapons are characteristic of Tantric guardian imagery. Inside, according to tradition, lies a mandala …

lore.title: Rituals for Rain
lore.excerpt: Shantipur's most famous ritual role is associated with rain. In times of drought, Newar Buddhist priests have historically performed ceremonies here to appeal to the nagas and bring the monsoon, continuing the tradition recorded in Pratap Malla's inscription. …

lore.title: Protecting a Sealed Sanctuary
lore.excerpt: Shantipur's conservation is shaped by its sealed chambers and its restricted ritual use. The building was damaged in the 2015 earthquake along with other structures on the hilltop, and repairs focused on stabilising its walls and roof without disturbing the in…

monuments.audioHook: This plain little building on the north side of the hill hides one of the strangest stories in Kathmandu. Behind its painted guardians, legend says, a great Tantric master named Shantikar sits in an underground chamber, meditating since ancient times to protect the sacred flame of Swayambhu. In the seventeenth century,…
monuments.nepaliSummary: शान्तिपुर स्वयम्भू डाँडाको तान्त्रिक तीर्थ हो, जहाँ राजा प्रताप मल्ल खडेरीमा वर्षाको मण्डल खोज्न भित्र पसेको अभिलेख छ।
monuments.talkingPoint: Tell the story of Pratap Malla's descent for the rain mandala.

monuments.century: present shrines of Malla and later centuries; cult far older
features: small shrine on the wooded western hillock of Swayambhu
pens, notebooks and offerings left by students
monuments.disambiguationTip: Manjushree's shrine stands on the separate western hillock among trees; the Vasubandhu chorten sits on the main stupa platform.

lore.title: The Bodhisattva Who Drained the Lake
lore.excerpt: On the smaller hillock west of the main Swayambhu stupa stands a shrine dedicated to Manjushri, the bodhisattva of wisdom, who is honoured in Newar tradition as a founding figure of the Kathmandu Valley. The Swayambhu Purana tells that Manjushri came from the …

lore.title: A Shrine Among Trees

lore.title: Sword of Wisdom, Book of Knowledge
